papers.title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
papers.summary: Over the past decade, substantial efforts have been devoted to developing machine learning (ML) methods for extracting materials data and, where possible, materials knowledge directly from the scientific literature. This review traces the evolution of these methods from heuristic, rule-based pipelines through natural language processing (NLP) models and transformer-based encoders to, lastly, large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems capable of extracting materials information across multiple modalities, including text, tables, and figures. Beside construction of large, queryable materials databases and knowledge graphs that support downstream materials discovery, we discuss how these advances have enabled new capabilities, such as, generic question answering across materials science, AI co-scientists and chatbots for research assistance, and closed-loop optimization and discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories. We critically assess the datasets generated using these approaches, their extraction accuracy and computational costs, and the respective strengths and limitations of different methodologies, and even provide practical guidelines for developing more reliable and scalable materials data extraction pipelines. Finally, we identify key open challenges, including the extraction of full materials structure-property-processing-performance tetrahedron at the sample level, the scarcity of reliable benchmark datasets for systematic evaluation, and the resolution of non-standard materials terminology across different document modalities.
papers.title_zh: 使用机器学习和大语言模型进行自动化材料数据与知识提取
papers.abstract_zh: 在过去的十年中，人们投入了大量努力来开发机器学习（ML）方法，用于直接从科学文献中提取材料数据，并在可能的情况下提取材料知识。本综述追溯了这些方法的演变：从启发式、基于规则的流程，经过自然语言处理（NLP）模型和基于 Transformer 的编码器，最后发展到能够跨多种模态（包括文本、表格和图）提取材料信息的大语言模型（LLM）和智能体系统。除了构建支持下游材料发现的大型可查询材料数据库和知识图谱外，我们还讨论了这些进展如何催生了新的能力，例如跨材料科学的通用问答、用于研究辅助的 AI 共同科学家和聊天机器人，以及在与自主实验室集成时实现的闭环优化与发现。我们批判性地评估了使用这些方法生成的数据集、其提取准确性和计算成本，以及不同方法各自的优势和局限性，甚至提供了用于开发更可靠、更可扩展的材料数据提取流程的实用指南。最后，我们指出了关键的开放挑战，包括在样品层面提取完整的材料结构-性质-加工-性能四面体、用于系统评估的可靠基准数据集稀缺，以及解决不同文档模态之间非标准材料术语的问题。

papers.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
papers.summary: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. We introduce Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed for measuring how far today's agents can improve the published best models on scientific ML benchmarks, spanning 20 benchmarks across 11 domains. Rather than ranking agents on a leaderboard, Agent4Sci asks what kinds of progress agents can make on these tasks under in-the-wild conditions, and where they fall short. Empirically, today's frontier agents advance the published best on every benchmark, with Claude Opus reaching 10.4% mean relative improvement and no run flagged for academic misconduct. These gains, however, come almost entirely from a bag of ML-engineering tricks rather than research-level insight. Trajectory analysis surfaces three recurring limitations in this setting: novelty miscalibration, resource under-utilization, and rapid collapse into local engineering sweeps. Lightweight plug-in skills for research ideation, experiment management, and scheduled checklists raise Claude Opus from 10.4% to 20.1% and Codex from 4.4% to 8.1%, while yielding more diverse, domain-relevant interventions. Agent4Sci gives the community a way to track and push frontier agents from ML engineering toward domain insight on real-world ML-for-science problems. Code and data are available on GitHub (https://github.com/maszhongming/agent4sci) and Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/datasets/MingZhong/agent4sci).

papers.title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
papers.summary: Agentic harness evolution optimizes an agent's instructions, tools, and control flow by using its task execution experiences as evolving evidence. While more evolution tasks should intuitively improve performance, our preliminary study reveals a paradoxical failure mode: the performance of existing methods degrades as the task pool expands. Our further analysis demonstrates that this degradation stems from suboptimal evidence selection during optimization, as different evidence combinations lead to substantially different evolution outcomes. To address this issue, we propose Successive Scale Racing (SSR), a framework that adaptively searches for optimal evidence combinations in each evolution round. SSR constructs diverse evidence combinations based on the corresponding task quality and coverage, and efficiently races the resulting candidate harnesses under a small compute budget. Empirically, across three distinct benchmarks, SSR achieves state-of-the-art results in all six configurations. Notably, as the task pool grows from 40 to 200, SSR steadily improves the pass rate from 64.3% to 68.3%, while the baselines' performances all drop. Furthermore, its racing mechanism identifies near-optimal candidates while reducing validation executions by 60%.

papers.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
papers.summary: Automated judges of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) outputs are necessary, but large language model (LLM) judges are costly and slow at scale. We compared Jev, a decision language model that returns structured judgments, with frontier and open-weight LLM judges in four use cases. On 118 pediatric answers, Jev's agreement with physicians' ordinal quality ratings (Gwet's AC2 0.50; expected score 0.53) matched or exceeded that of seven of 12 LLM judges, including frontier models, Claude Opus 5.5 (0.49) and GPT-6 (0.38). On physician-graded binary HealthBench criteria, Jev matched or exceeded four of six LLM judges. On MedHELM's open-ended tasks, Jev's agreement with a three-LLM jury approached or exceeded the jurors' internal agreement. On HealthBench Professional, Jev matched the benchmark's reference judge, GPT-5.4, on 91% of criteria (other judges, 91-93%). Frontier judges cost 73-294 times more than Jev and took 7-57 times longer. Jev may enable efficient clinical AI evaluation at scale.
papers.title_zh: 决策语言模型作为临床生成式 AI 的 LLM 评判者的可负担且快速的替代方案
papers.abstract_zh: 对临床人工智能（AI）输出进行自动化评判是必要的，但大型语言模型（LLM）评判者在大规模应用时成本高昂且速度缓慢。我们在四个用例中，将 Jev——一种返回结构化判断的决策语言模型——与前沿和开放权重 LLM 评判者进行了比较。在 118 个儿科回答上，Jev 与医生有序质量评分的一致性（Gwet's AC2 0.50；期望得分 0.53）达到或超过 12 个 LLM 评判者中 7 个的一致性，包括前沿模型 Claude Opus 5.5（0.49）和 GPT-6（0.38）。在由医生评分的二元 HealthBench 标准上，Jev 达到或超过六个 LLM 评判者中四个的表现。在 MedHELM 的开放式任务上，Jev 与由三个 LLM 组成的评审团的一致性接近或超过评审团成员内部的一致性。在 HealthBench Professional 上，Jev 在 91% 的标准上与基准的参考评判者 GPT-5.4 相匹配（其他评判者为 91-93%）。前沿评判者的成本是 Jev 的 73-294 倍，耗时是 Jev 的 7-57 倍。Jev 可能使规模化临床 AI 评估实现高效。

papers.title: Sketch2Sim: an end-to-end modular framework for hand-drawn circuit analysis
papers.summary: This study proposes a sketch-to-simulation system to solve handwritten circuit diagrams. The system converts raw images into a Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (SPICE)-compatible netlist and automatically calculates the circuit's nodal voltages and currents. Another objective is to propose a holistic framework that benefits students and educators by enhancing the teaching and learning experience of electric circuits and expediting engineering design reviews. This article presents a multistage pipeline that converts raw photographs of handwritten electric circuits into executable SPICE-like netlists, providing a solution. A dataset of 1,000 hand-drawn Resistor-Inductor-Capacitor (RLC) circuits was curated and annotated for components, text regions, and character recognition. The proposed system decomposes a circuit diagram into three stages: (i) dual You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detectors for components and text regions, (ii) a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) and Optical Character Recognition (OCR)-based domain-aware symbol value extraction, and (iii) image processing with thresholding, skeletonization, and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) to automatically identify nodes and map them with corresponding components. The proposed system produces the netlist and solves the circuit. The qualitative and quantitative ablation studies on modular stages, as well as end-to-end tests, demonstrate robust performance across various handwriting styles, lighting conditions, and clutter.This study serves as an interactive learning aid and practical tool for professionals, providing a comprehensive user interface (UI), enabling rapid digitization of circuit sketches for study, design, prototyping, or troubleshooting.

papers.title: Speedrunning Relational Foundation Model Pretraining
papers.summary: Progress on foundation model pretraining is gated by who can afford a trial, and relational pretraining is no exception. Recipes are developed inside individual labs, reported under private protocols, and do not accumulate. Speedrun leaderboards remove that barrier by decentralizing the search rather than the training run. The problem is fixed, the stack is open, entries are ranked by wall-clock time to a quality target, and one GPU is enough to hold the record. We introduce modded-nanoRT, the first such leaderboard for Relational Transformers. Which database to hold out decides whether the benchmark can resolve improvements at all, so we fix it by calibration, ranking six candidates by how sharply a 45-minute learning curve separates improvement from seed noise. We open the leaderboard with typed trilinear attention, a relational operator that conditions attention scores and values on the foreign key traversed, together with Muon and SIGReg. The recipe reaches the target in 305.63 seconds on one NVIDIA H200, 8.11x faster than the reference implementation, and wins 13 of 15 pairs outside the development database. We will release the benchmark, its frozen artifacts, and the record runs. Our code is available at https://github.com/kunumi/nanoRT.
authors: Gabriel Wedson Mendonça de Souza Veloso

papers.title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
papers.summary: Large language models increasingly take part in extended conversations where they can both shape and be shaped by another party's views, yet most persuasion research measures only one side of that exchange. We introduce a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework in which two language-model roles repeatedly discuss a contested topic (climate-change attribution): one is given an assigned stance and, in some conditions, an explicit instruction to persuade, while the other receives no assigned position. Across four ordered model combinations involving GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, we track both each role's explicitly reported position and a separate measure of its turn-by-turn behavior inside the conversation. Opinion dynamics differ substantially across model combinations: same-model interactions narrow the opinion gap on average, clearly for only one of the two models, while cross-model interactions widen it. Explicit reports and in-dialogue behavior capture distinct aspects of opinion dynamics, and a blanket instruction to persuade does not reliably increase influence. These findings suggest that conversational influence depends not only on assigned roles and initial positions but also on the participating models, with implications for how opinion change is measured in extended LLM interactions.
papers.title_zh: 操纵还是不操纵：LLM 交互中的观点动力学
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型越来越多地参与到长时间的对话中，在这些对话里它们既能塑造另一方的观点，也会被另一方的观点所塑造，然而大多数说服研究只测量了这一交互过程的一侧。我们引入了一个受控的 LLM-LLM 辩论框架，其中两个语言模型角色就一个有争议的话题（气候变化归因）反复讨论：其中一个被赋予指定立场，并在某些条件下被明确指示去说服对方，而另一个则没有被赋予任何立场。在涉及 GPT-6 Luna 与 Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite 的四种有序模型组合中，我们同时追踪每个角色明确报告的位置，以及对其在对话中逐轮行为的另一项独立测量。观点动力学在不同模型组合之间差异显著：同模型交互平均而言缩小了观点差距，且仅对两个模型中的一个表现得明显，而跨模型交互则扩大了该差距。明确报告与对话内行为捕捉了观点动力学的不同方面，而一概而论的说服指令并不能可靠地增加影响力。这些发现表明，对话中的影响不仅取决于被分配的角色和初始立场，还取决于参与其中的模型，这对于如何在长时间的 LLM 交互中测量观点变化具有启示意义。

papers.title: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
papers.summary: Many social evaluations for multiagent systems study behaviors as they emerge from environments instead of systematically intervening in the environment to elicit such behaviors. We introduce Fig (Finding Interactions in Games), an agentic system that performs targeted elicitation interventions on game environments. It takes a natural language behavior description, decomposes it into sub-behaviors, generates new social games or selects existing ones, and executes single or combined interventions to the games' engine, opponents, instructions, and context. To evaluate model behavior, it combines built-in mechanical checks and synthetic rubric judgments. We validate the interventions, generated games, and evaluation mechanisms via human review. Models attempt the target behavior in 45.2% of episodes on average for valid scenarios generated by Fig for six test behaviors -- cooperation, exploitation, deception, covert coordination, betrayal, and sabotage. For game-behavior pairs with available controls, Fig's interventions increase attempt rates by 10.9% on average compared to matched control games. Fig shows that multiagent environments can serve as programmable test beds for intentional, controllable, and reproducible behavior evaluation. Code is available at https://github.com/fleet-ai/fig.

papers.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
papers.summary: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means. In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors; the receiver consumes them while retaining its own context, canvas, and trajectory. Removing a message tests whether the channel matters; replacing it with a message from another example tests whether its content matters. Across controlled tasks, derangement removes a +63.6-point advantage on Tiny-A2D and a +100.0-point advantage on Dream-7B, while targeted substitutions steer the receiver toward the substituted fact. On QASC with the two supporting facts split across agents, matched communication reaches 80.8%, but a wrong-example message lowers accuracy to 46.8%, a content effect of +34.0 points. The surprising result is temporal: one late transfer reaches 87.8%, exceeding four recurrent exchanges by +7.0 points. These experiments provide causal evidence for continuous hidden communication between diffusion-LM agents and show that when information is transferred can matter more than how many times agents exchange it.
papers.title_zh: 扩散语言模型智能体之间的隐藏消息：潜在通信的因果证据
papers.abstract_zh: 扩散语言模型通过一系列可修正的连续状态形成答案，但多智能体系统通常会丢弃这些状态，只让智能体在解码出文本之后才进行通信。我们追问：一条独立的扩散轨迹能否将一条紧凑的隐藏消息传递给另一条轨迹，并且更关键的是，接收方是否会使用该消息所表达的含义。在 Hidden Messages 中，发送方将其去噪状态压缩为四个带符号的稠密向量；接收方在消费这些向量的同时保留自身的上下文、画布与轨迹。移除一条消息可检验该通道是否有影响；将其替换为来自另一个样本的消息则可检验其内容是否有影响。在一系列受控任务中，错配消除了 Tiny-A2D 上 +63.6 点的优势以及 Dream-7B 上 +100.0 点的优势，而有针对性的替换则会将接收方引导至被替换进来的事实。在将两个支撑事实拆分到不同智能体上的 QASC 任务中，匹配的通信达到 80.8%，但一条来自错误样本的消息会将准确率降至 46.8%，即 +34.0 点的内容效应。令人惊讶的结果是时间性的：一次较晚的传递达到 87.8%，比四次循环交换高出 +7.0 点。这些实验为扩散语言模型智能体之间的连续隐藏通信提供了因果证据，并表明信息在何时被传递，可能比智能体交换信息的次数更为重要。

papers.title: DiffResearch: Accelerating Deep Research with Diffusion Language Models
papers.summary: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use. Almost all production systems are built on autoregressive (AR) language models and inherit left-to-right decoding in planning and long-form writing. We present DiffResearch, an open multi-agent deep research framework that places a diffusion language model (dLLM) at the core of every stage, and measure how a diffusion backbone changes latency and report quality. Holding the agentic scaffold, retrieval code, prompts, and evaluation fixed, we swap the backbone between an open diffusion model and a comparable AR model. Across 100 Deep Research Bench tasks, the diffusion backbone is roughly 6 times faster end-to-end, driven by order-of-magnitude reductions in planning and writing. We further introduce dFast, a decomposition mode that reads intermediate denoising states and extracts subqueries before generation finishes, providing a 1.99 times median speedup for decomposition in isolation with no loss of report quality. On the benchmark's RACE rubric, dFast obtains the best overall score among the three configurations. Finally, in a public system-level leaderboard snapshot, an instance built on a stronger diffusion model ranks above several commercial systems. We release DiffResearch under an Apache-2.0 license.
papers.title_zh: DiffResearch：利用扩散语言模型加速深度研究
papers.abstract_zh: 深度研究系统迭代地规划、收集证据、综合和修订，使得端到端延迟成为交互式使用的一个关键瓶颈。几乎所有生产系统都构建在自回归（AR）语言模型之上，并在规划和长文本写作中继承从左到右的解码方式。我们提出 DiffResearch，一个开放的多智能体深度研究框架，它将扩散语言模型（dLLM）置于每个阶段的核心，并衡量扩散骨干如何改变延迟和报告质量。在保持智能体脚手架、检索代码、提示词和评估不变的情况下，我们在一个开放扩散模型和一个可比的 AR 模型之间替换骨干。在 100 个 Deep Research Bench 任务上，扩散骨干的端到端速度约快 6 倍，这由规划和写作环节耗时降低一个数量级所驱动。我们进一步引入 dFast，一种分解模式，它读取中间去噪状态，并在生成完成前提取子查询，在孤立分解任务上提供 1.99 倍的中位加速，且不损失报告质量。在该基准的 RACE 评分标准上，dFast 在三种配置中获得最佳总体得分。最后，在一个公开的系统级排行榜快照中，一个构建在更强扩散模型上的实例排名高于若干商业系统。我们以 Apache-2.0 许可证发布 DiffResearch。

papers.title: Simply Logical -- The First Three Decades
papers.summary: This paper charts the evolution of the Prolog textbook Simply Logical -- Intelligent Reasoning by Example from print with runnable programmes on a 3.5-inch diskette published in 1994, via various intermediate online versions, to the fully interactive online edition available today. Our aim is to investigate -- from both the writer's and the reader's perspectives -- the potential impact of technology on educational materials. The three authors of this paper present three distinct and complementary points of view, which come together to shape an interactive online book that offers an immersive learning experience. Peter describes the philosophy behind the original book and experiences teaching from it. Jan demonstrates how contemporary web programming has enabled a fully interactive realisation of the book's philosophy. Kacper reports how different technologies can be adopted to build a versatile authoring toolkit that underpins the interactive online edition of the book. Collating these distinct yet coherent perspectives allows us to reflect on future opportunities for interactive Prolog teaching materials arising from the continuous development of web technologies. The insights we offer should be of interest to teachers of Prolog as well as those wanting to find out about the latest educational technologies.

papers.title: D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills
papers.summary: Frontier language-model agents excel at complex tasks, but high inference costs make transferring their capabilities to smaller models essential. Traditional knowledge distillation achieves this through parameter updates, requiring access to the student's weights and additional training compute while encoding the transferred knowledge implicitly in the parameters. We introduce D-Skill, a framework that treats the teacher as a black box and distills its behavioral advantage into an interpretable natural-language skill by analyzing paired rollouts and identifying behavioral divergences and agreements. The resulting lessons are consolidated offline, with any compatible skill-update backend, into a skill document that is provided to the student at inference time. D-Skill constructs the skill entirely offline from fixed trajectories, without labels, further environment interaction, or weight updates after rollout collection. Across SpreadsheetBench-Verified, ALFWorld, and chess puzzles spanning multiple teacher-student pairs, D-Skill closes 75%-95% of the teacher-student gap without touching model weights. After a single offline pass over the paired traces, D-Skill outperforms one-epoch SFT baselines and remains competitive with multi-epoch SFT. Under the same model family, the resulting student also incurs 5.7x-8.3x lower inference cost per task than the teacher. Our results demonstrate that natural-language skill distillation offers a performant, interpretable, and efficient alternative to weight-based capability transfer.

papers.title: Back Up Before You Regret: Measuring Backup Awareness and Automating Backup in Coding Agents
papers.summary: Coding agents now complete tasks autonomously, modifying real-world state such as artifacts, software environments, and configurations along the way. Yet they show limited backup awareness: recognizing that an action will modify state that may later be needed, and preserving it beforehand. To evaluate backup awareness, we introduce RegretBench, a benchmark of 205 executable tasks grounded in regret moments reported on platforms such as X.com, GitHub, and Stack Overflow, where users explicitly regretted not preserving state they later needed. Across six frontier models, agents complete 86.1% of tasks on average yet back up before these moments in only 15.2%, showing that task completion ability does not imply backup awareness. Because it is hard to predict which changes will be regretted, we propose BackUpper, a harness plug-in backup layer that checks every tool call and preserves affected state before modification. It combines rule-based strategies for common operations with a lightweight subagent for complex cases, and its rule table can expand with subagent decisions over time. On RegretBench, BackUpper covers every regret moment action and restores states with 92.2% average similarity to the original. Achieving this costs only $0.014 per task, with 7x fewer tokens than the main-agent self-backup baseline. When users have preferences on what to back up, BackUpper can also narrow its scope accordingly, matching human annotations on whether an action is worth preserving with an 84.5% F1 score. These results suggest that agents can keep actions reversible at low cost while respecting users' preferences.

papers.title: Self-Improving Agents with World Model Predictive Paths
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to interact with environments and improve their decisions during deployment. However, how anticipating future outcomes and drawing on accumulated interaction experience can jointly support decision-making remains underexplored. We propose a test-time framework, inspired by Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control, that combines multi-branch predictive analysis with experience-based adaptation. At each step, the agent proposes multiple candidate actions and imagines their outcomes with a world model, so that alternatives can be compared without being executed in the environment. Since language environments provide neither explicit dynamics nor costs, the predicted outcomes are evaluated for task progress and risk, and MPPI-style weights over the resulting costs guide the final decision. A dual-branch experience memory enables self-improvement: the planner branch refines candidate generation and action selection, while the world model branch improves next-observation prediction. Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld across three backbones demonstrate the strong overall performance of our method and the effectiveness of experience-guided predictive control. Our code will be made publicly available.
papers.title_zh: 基于世界模型预测路径的自我改进智能体
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体日益被期望与环境交互，并在部署过程中改进其决策。然而，预判未来结果与利用积累的交互经验如何共同支持决策仍未被充分探索。我们提出一个受模型预测路径积分（MPPI）控制启发的测试时框架，它将多分支预测分析与基于经验的自适应相结合。在每一步，智能体提出多个候选动作，并用世界模型想象它们的结果，从而可以在不于环境中执行的情况下比较各种备选方案。由于语言环境既不提供显式动力学也不提供代价，预测结果会针对任务进展和风险进行评估，而基于所得代价的 MPPI 风格权重会引导最终决策。双分支经验记忆实现了自我改进：规划器分支改进候选生成和动作选择，而世界模型分支改进下一观测预测。在 ALFWorld 和 ScienceWorld 上跨三个骨干模型的实验证明了我们方法的强大整体性能以及经验引导的预测控制的有效性。我们的代码将公开提供。

papers.title: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
papers.summary: While large language models are increasingly deployed as tool-calling agents, their safety evaluations still focus primarily on their ability to refuse harmful requests in text. We investigate whether the refusal behavior in text transfers to tool use. We construct a benchmark of 2,304 prompts across four domains, consisting of matched triplets that present the same harmful or benign request in text-only, standard tool-enabled, and adversarially framed tool-enabled settings. We then assess tool-call safety using 20 predefined forbidden actions. Testing five models of varying sizes and families, we find that requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls. Under standard tool-enabled prompting, this divergence occurs for 10-52 percent of harmful requests refused in chat. To mechanistically investigate this gap, we identify a refusal-associated direction in the residual stream of each of the five models. We find that in tool-enabled contexts, the activations along this direction decrease in four of five models. Furthermore, lower activation predicts unsafe tool calls across all five models (AUC 0.76-0.86). However, restoring the signal to the respective text-only value through activation patching only prevents a subset of unsafe calls, primarily by suppressing tool use rather than by producing safer calls. Steering along the refusal direction nearly eliminates unsafe calls only at strengths that also suppress benign tool use or degrade the output quality. Our findings indicate that the identified refusal direction contributes to whether a model acts, but only partially explains the refusal divergence. Therefore, evaluating the safety of tool-calling agents requires directly examining their actions along with their textual responses.
papers.title_zh: 超越文本的行为：评估 LLM 智能体中拒绝迁移失败
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管大语言模型正越来越多地被部署为工具调用智能体，但其安全评估仍主要关注其在文本中拒绝有害请求的能力。我们研究文本中的拒绝行为是否会迁移到工具使用中。我们构建了一个包含 2,304 个提示、覆盖四个领域的基准，由匹配的三元组组成，这些三元组分别在纯文本、标准启用工具以及对抗性框架的启用工具设置中呈现相同的有害或良性请求。随后，我们使用 20 个预定义的禁止动作来评估工具调用安全性。在测试五个规模和家族各异的模型后，我们发现，在文本中被拒绝的请求常常导致不安全的工具调用。在标准启用工具提示下，这种分歧发生在聊天中被拒绝的有害请求的 10% 至 52% 中。为了从机制上研究这一差距，我们在五个模型各自的残差流中识别出一个与拒绝相关的方向。我们发现，在启用工具的上下文中，沿该方向的激活在五个模型中的四个中下降。此外，较低的激活可预测所有五个模型中的不安全工具调用（AUC 0.76–0.86）。然而，通过激活修补将该信号恢复到相应的纯文本值，只能阻止一部分不安全调用，而且主要是通过抑制工具使用，而不是通过产生更安全的调用来实现。沿拒绝方向进行引导，只有在强度同时会抑制良性工具使用或降低输出质量时，才几乎消除不安全调用。我们的发现表明，所识别出的拒绝方向有助于解释模型是否采取行动，但只能部分解释拒绝行为的分歧。因此，评估工具调用智能体的安全性需要直接检查其行动及其文本响应。

papers.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
papers.summary: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. We present PerMIT, a memory architecture with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption: only user-typed inputs and values confirmed at a gate are trusted. PerMIT mediates the release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, while preserving agent-driven multi-turn planning and tool choice. Over this finite interface, we prove two integrity theorems that are also machine-checked in Lean 4, which together ensure that environment-derived memory reaches a sensitive action only if confirmed at the gate and influences the agent's behavior only through what the gate displays. Every attack in our threat model thereby reduces to a single auditable decision, which a human, an LLM verifier, or both can make in practice. On Trojan Hippo, PerMIT records zero observed attack success with self-verification and lightweight verifiers. Because each confirmation is a logged verdict on exact content, endorsements accumulate across users, and sufficiently endorsed items become community-confirmed with no further verification required. Under explicit assumptions, we prove and corroborate in simulation a co-scaling property: as the community grows, the risks of promoting poison and of wrongly evicting benign knowledge fall, while per-user verification effort does not rise. On $τ^2$-bench, communities of up to 90 autonomous agents use PerMIT to build shared knowledge bases with no direct memory injection promoted, and the resulting knowledge significantly improves new agents on held-out tasks, suggesting a path toward agents that safely self-improve at test time.

papers.title: AgentPolicyForge: From Executable Environments to Policy Benchmarks and Adaptive Guards
papers.summary: Customized agent deployments define policies over tools, resources, and execution conditions. Providing these policies in the task agent's prompt does not reliably prevent violations. Training a guard requires examples of tool calls that comply with or violate those policies. We introduce AgentPolicyForge, a framework that uses executable environments to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train policy guards. With this framework, we construct PolicyGym, a dataset across ten policy families using 698 scenarios for training data generation and 254 separate held-out scenarios for human-reviewed test sets. Tool calls are executed and their outcomes recorded to help determine whether they comply with the policy. Every violating case uses a permitted tool, requiring checks of arguments, resources, and context rather than tool identity alone. The case construction process supports iterative guard training: an attacker generates requests using retrieved strategies, and the guard is fine-tuned on balanced, environment-verified examples. Training improves policy enforcement even with a fixed archive. Updating the archive further reduces in-domain attack success compared with keeping it fixed. We compare policy-aware task agent self-regulation with a trained policy guard. On PolicyGym, the final guard-based configuration achieves a 40-44% relative reduction in attack success rate and fewer benign rejections than policy prompting alone.

papers.title: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning
papers.summary: Radiation treatment planning requires balancing competing objectives to satisfy clinical criteria while accommodating physicians' preferences. This study aims to develop an evidence-driven, multi-agent compound AI system that integrates DRL-based automated treatment planning with LLM-based conversational plan refinement for proton PBS therapy. A policy network trained using PPO first generates multiple plans without human intervention, from which one is selected as the target plan and the others serve as references for subsequent refinements. For challenging cases requiring further adjustments, an LLM-based multi-agent system enables plan refinement through natural language interactions. The system comprises a planning agent that recommends evidence-supported adjustments, a chatbot providing a unified conversational interface, and an evaluation agent that retrieves clinical metrics and identifies constraint violations. To enhance domain-specific reasoning, the planning agent based on Qwen3-14B is designed to justify its recommendations using evidence from previously generated plans and post-trained on task-specific data using SFT and GRPO. The framework was trained and evaluated using 21 patients with H&N cancers, with 5 PPO-generated plans per patient. Of these, 50 plans were selected for instruction-guided refinement. Compared with the base LLM, the post-trained Qwen3-14B demonstrated improved instruction-following, information retrieval and domain-specific reasoning capabilities. The resulting adjustments more effectively improved user-prioritized objectives while limiting deterioration in competing objectives, yielding more clinically appropriate trade-offs in patient-specific plan refinement. The proposed compound AI system provides a user-friendly planning platform, offering a promising approach to personalized proton PBS treatment planning.

papers.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
papers.summary: Coding agents are rapidly advancing from single-file generation to long-horizon repository-scale engineering, yet the evaluation of their capabilities to author interactive extended reality (XR) applications remains an open challenge. Unlike traditional software, XR applications operate within dynamic 3D physical environments where runtime robustness depends jointly on continuous user motion, spatial input, and environmental sensing. We introduce GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark for the end-to-end evaluation of coding agents in XR software development. GenXR-Bench contains 112 expert-authored tasks spanning 24 feature implementations, 21 bug repairs, and 67 application generation tasks. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interactions with programmatic and visual assertions to evaluate core functionality and runtime behavior. GenXR-Bench's testing suite achieves 96.5% accuracy against blinded expert judgments of 124 candidate applications executed on consumer XR hardware. Evaluating 10 models on GenXR-Bench, we find that the strongest configuration achieves only 50.9% overall Pass@1. Failure analysis identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics. GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing.

papers.title: Inheritance as an Admission Test for LLM Prompt Merge Operators
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are often improved by iterating until a fixed verifier is done. Once that verifier saturates, the loop has nothing left to climb. We instead score agents against the current population, and a frozen panel records whether anyone got better. The panel mean can rise inside the seeds by elimination alone. We therefore count a run as training only when its final mean beats the best generation-zero member. A merge is admitted only when the child moves toward the donor, past the child the same operator produces at zero dose, and the lower confidence bound on that movement reaches half the requested dose. That is the admission test. A detectable shortfall rejects the operator, and the test is otherwise undetermined. We keep realised fitness φas the selector and reference performance θas the unused ruler. Every measurement uses gemini-3.1-flash-lite on one negotiation task, and no fixed-oracle arm was run. In the open loop, tactic append grafts short donor rules and is admitted. Free rewrite moves only a third of the requested dose and is rejected. Template append pastes raw donor replies into the child. Its movement clears the bound on the first probe but not on the re-probe, and it is left undetermined. A held-out re-probe on the five situations the merge never saw confirms that both appends move, and it does not rescue free rewrite. Neither append rises with the dose. Constrained rewrite is admitted in the open loop and was not run in the closed loop, which changes only the operator. The population, the scores and the task stay fixed. No free-rewrite run beats the best generation-zero member. Every tactic-append run and every template-append run does. Sampled loop children keep that split. Free rewrite moves no further toward the donor, and both appends still clear the bound, by less than in the open loop.
papers.title_zh: 继承作为 LLM 提示合并算子的准入测试
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通常通过迭代直到固定验证器完成而得到改进。一旦该验证器饱和，循环就没有可继续攀升的空间。我们改为针对当前种群给智能体打分，并由一个冻结面板记录是否有人变得更好。仅通过淘汰，面板均值就可以在种子内部上升。因此，只有当一个运行的最终均值超过最佳第零代成员时，我们才将其计为训练。仅当子代朝供体移动、越过同一算子在零剂量下产生的子代，并且该移动的置信下界达到所请求剂量的一半时，合并才被准入。这就是准入测试。可检测到的不足会拒绝该算子，否则测试为未确定。我们保留实际适应度 φas 作为选择器，并保留参考性能 θas 作为未使用的标尺。每次测量都在一个谈判任务上使用 gemini-3.1-flash-lite，且未运行固定预言机臂。在开环中，策略追加移植简短的供体规则并被准入。自由重写仅移动所请求剂量的三分之一，并被拒绝。模板追加将原始供体回复粘贴到子代中。其移动在第一次探测中越过边界，但在再次探测中没有，因此它被留作未确定。对合并从未见过的五个情境进行的留出再探测确认两种追加都会移动，并且它不能挽救自由重写。两种追加都不随剂量上升。约束重写在开环中被准入，且未在闭环中运行，闭环仅改变算子。种群、分数和任务保持固定。没有任何自由重写运行超过最佳第零代成员。每个策略追加运行和每个模板追加运行都超过了。采样的循环子代保持该分化。自由重写没有进一步朝供体移动，而两种追加仍然越过边界，但幅度小于开环中。

papers.title: GRAIL: From Saliency to Semantics in Time-Series Explanation
papers.summary: Explaining a time-series model requires both locating the evidence and extracting meaningful knowledge from it. Yet a single timestep is not a semantic unit: the meaningful patterns live across many samples, not in any one of them. Per-timestep saliency is therefore noisy, high-dimensional, and unstable. Existing methods address this by introducing fixed-size windows and treating them as independent players in a cooperative game. Evaluating a coalition of such players requires defining a ``baseline'' region, which prior work tackles with fixed counterfactuals (e.g., a flat line, noise, or a spectral surrogate). This choice frequently dominates the resulting explanation, obscuring the model's true decisions. To address these issues, we propose GRAIL, a region-based time-series explanation framework that uses domain-specific intervals, such as the P-wave and the QRS complex of an electrocardiogram (ECG) beat, as players. We describe each region with human-readable features and generate counterfactual baselines with an on-manifold conditional generator. Such a choice of players also admits non-temporal features: static covariates enter as singleton players attributed with the temporal regions on one scale, so a patient's tabular evidence (e.g., age, sex) is weighed directly against the signal. We attribute the predictions to the features via Owen values with common-random-number variance reduction. Experimental results on both synthetic and real data show that the proposed framework produces faithful and robust explanations, evaluated under matched on- and off-manifold operators, offering meaningful knowledge to domain experts.

papers.title: AutoFraming: Synthesizing Dynamic Frames of C Code with LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown considerable promise in synthesizing formal specifications from source code. However, existing approaches primarily focus on functional contracts and loop invariants, while largely neglecting frame conditions, which specify the memory locations that may or may not be modified during execution and constitute an essential part of formal specifications. To address this limitation, we propose an LLM-based approach for synthesizing ACSL frame specifications alongside functional contracts from C code. Our approach analyzes code property graphs (CPGs) to extract frame-relevant information from the input code and leverages this information to guide the LLM in generating accurate frame conditions. The resulting specifications capture both region-separation constraints and data dependencies that govern variable modifications. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. On a benchmark of 84 ACSL-compliant functions from non-trivial real-world systems, our method successfully synthesizes error-free frame specifications for 92.9% of the functions, representing a 179% relative improvement over state-of-the-art techniques. On a second benchmark consisting of 51 functions, the success rate increases from 80.4% to 96.1%. Furthermore, when integrated as an auxiliary component into existing LLM-based ACSL-synthesis frameworks, our approach improves frame-specification generation performance by up to 61.9%.
papers.title_zh: AutoFraming：使用LLMs合成C代码的动态帧
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在从源代码合成形式化规约方面已展现出相当大的前景。然而，现有方法主要关注功能契约和循环不变式，而在很大程度上忽略了帧条件，帧条件规定了在执行期间可能被修改或不得被修改的内存位置，并且构成形式化规约的重要组成部分。为解决这一局限，我们提出一种基于LLM的方法，用于从C代码合成ACSL帧规约以及功能契约。我们的方法分析代码属性图（CPGs），以从输入代码中提取与帧相关的信息，并利用这些信息指导LLM生成准确的帧条件。所得到的规约同时捕获支配变量修改的区域分离约束和数据依赖。实验结果表明了我们方法的有效性。在来自非平凡真实世界系统的84个符合ACSL的函数的基准上，我们的方法成功为92.9%的函数合成了无错误的帧规约，相对于最先进技术实现了179%的相对提升。在由51个函数组成的第二个基准上，成功率从80.4%提高到96.1%。此外，当作为辅助组件集成到现有基于LLM的ACSL合成框架中时，我们的方法将帧规约生成性能最多提升61.9%。

papers.title: Does Every Instance Count Equally? Order Effects in LLM Multi-Instance Processing
papers.summary: Users increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to analyse collections of independent inputs, such as product reviews or social media posts, and return a single aggregated answer. This setting requires multi-instance processing (MIP), where a model combines information from multiple instances into one prediction. We study a task in which the model must infer a binary label for each instance, and identify the most frequent label among the full instance set. The correct answer should be invariant to instance order. By evaluating fifteen LLMs across five datasets and seven instance order patterns, with each instance set held fixed across patterns, we find substantial order sensitivity. Accuracy can differ by about 90 percentage points between the best and worst order patterns, with models generally more accurate when majority-label instances appear at the start than when they appear in the middle or at the end. For subsets of models, available reasoning traces and gradient-based attribution reveal uneven emphasis across positions. Traces disproportionately mention early instances, while attribution scores are generally higher near the beginning and end than in the middle. These results show that instance order can systematically bias aggregated predictions, highlighting the need to evaluate MIP across different input arrangements.
papers.title_zh: 每个实例都同等重要吗？LLM 多实例处理中的顺序效应
papers.abstract_zh: 用户越来越多地依赖大语言模型（LLM）来分析独立输入的集合，例如产品评论或社交媒体帖子，并返回一个单一的聚合答案。这一场景需要多实例处理（MIP），即模型将来自多个实例的信息整合为一个预测。我们研究了一项任务：模型必须为每个实例推断一个二值标签，并在完整实例集中识别出出现最频繁的标签。正确答案应当对实例顺序保持不变。通过在五个数据集和七种实例顺序模式上评估十五个 LLM，并在各模式之间保持每个实例集固定不变，我们发现存在显著的顺序敏感性。最佳与最差顺序模式之间的准确率可相差约 90 个百分点，且当多数标签实例出现在开头时，模型的准确率通常高于其出现在中间或末尾时。对于部分模型，可用的推理轨迹与基于梯度的归因揭示了不同位置之间不均衡的关注度。推理轨迹不成比例地提及较早的实例，而归因分数通常在开头和末尾附近高于中间。这些结果表明，实例顺序能够系统性地使聚合预测产生偏差，凸显了在不同输入排列下评估 MIP 的必要性。

papers.title: Context-Augmented, Session-Calibrated Blood Pressure Tracking from Photoplethysmography
papers.summary: Objective.To distinguish the contributions of acquisition context and photoplethysmography (PPG) to session-calibrated blood pressure (BP) tracking.Approach. The original comparison used three repeats of five-fold participant-level cross-validation in 653 AuroraBP participants, excluding calibration-labelled prediction targets. Matched analyses separated context and PPG and removed elapsed-time terms. Later exploratory follow-ups retained PPG, accelerometer signals and three initial cuff readings. Separate studies evaluated pulse-rate fusion and an intraoperative VitalDB model. Main results.The original wearable-state model achieved participant-level mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 7.697/6.139 mmHg for systolic/diastolic BP (SBP/DBP). Added context reduced MAE by 0.436/0.126 mmHg (97.5% intervals 0.305-0.573/0.053-0.200). In the matched factorial without the external PPG prior, PPG improved on calibration, time and protocol-provided posture/activity by 0.214/0.135 mmHg; removing time left the DBP interval including zero. Standard PPG descriptors contributed, but additional nonlinear/attractor benefit was not established. In a separate follow-up series, a sensor-history ensemble achieved 7.299/5.445 mmHg versus its static-rich reference's 7.363/5.470, small gains of 0.064/0.025 mmHg. Larger DBP errors did not improve uniformly. Quality-weighted fusion reduced pulse-rate MAE from 3.985 to 3.690 beats per minute. VitalDB MAEs remained 15.375/8.833 mmHg despite small PPG gains. Significance. The contribution is a calibrated evaluation framework with explicit controls, reproducible feature-cache-to-results analyses and retained negative findings. The sensor-history gain is exploratory after repeated dataset reuse. Independently estimated wearable states, complete raw-signal reproduction of the supplied richer features, external transfer and clinical adequacy remain unestablished.

papers.title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
papers.summary: Multilingual large language models are increasingly deployed in settings where visible reasoning traces support verification, education, and safety auditing, yet standard evaluations typically measure only final-answer agreement or holistic response similarity. As a result, they establish outcome consistency without determining whether users across languages receive comparable supporting evidence. We introduce a trace-level divergence framework that compares visible reasoning traces as structured sequences, decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity, with pair-specific calibration to enable comparison across languages. Across three reasoning benchmarks, seven languages, and six frontier LLMs, the natural baseline---embedding each whole response and comparing the two by cosine---systematically overstates agreement: $52.1\%$--$67.3\%$ of examples in the top quartile of holistic similarity are not in the top quartile of structural similarity. This dissociation is stable across sentence encoders and step segmentations, and blind bilingual annotation studies in two English-anchored language pairs show that human judgments align with structural similarity rather than with the holistic baseline. A same-language control shows that the level of divergence is language-specific: two English traces for paraphrases of the same question agree more closely than an English trace and its counterparts in other languages. Our results show that answer-level and holistic evaluations can substantially overestimate the consistency of multilingual explanatory artifacts, motivating trace-level evaluation for reliable multilingual deployment.
papers.title_zh: 相同答案，不同理由：多语言大语言模型中的轨迹级分歧
papers.abstract_zh: 多语言大语言模型越来越多地被部署在可见推理轨迹支持验证、教育和安全审计的场景中，然而标准评估通常只衡量最终答案一致性或整体响应相似度。因此，它们确立了结果一致性，却没有确定不同语言的用户是否获得可比的支持性证据。我们引入一个轨迹级分歧框架，该框架将可见推理轨迹作为结构化序列进行比较，把一致性分解为结构相似度、顺序一致性和整体相似度，并通过配对特定校准来实现跨语言比较。在三个推理基准、七种语言和六个前沿大语言模型上，自然基线——嵌入每个完整响应并通过余弦比较两者——系统性地高估了一致性：在整体相似度最高四分位数中的示例里，有 $52.1\%$--$67.3\%$ 不在结构相似度最高四分位数中。这种分离在句子编码器和步骤分割下保持稳定，并且在两个以英语为锚点的语言对中进行的盲双语标注研究表明，人类判断与结构相似度一致，而不是与整体基线一致。同语言对照表明，分歧水平具有语言特异性：针对同一问题改述的两个英语轨迹之间的一致性，高于一个英语轨迹与其在其他语言中的对应轨迹之间的一致性。我们的结果表明，答案级和整体评估可能大幅高估多语言解释性产物的一致性，这促使在多语言可靠部署中进行轨迹级评估。

papers.title: GRAM: Group-wise Rank-Aware Model Merging via Subspace Alignment
papers.summary: Merging different models into a single model is highly desirable for multi-task deployment, particularly in regulated domains like healthcare. In such settings, models are often locally fine-tuned due to strict data privacy policies, necessitating that aggregation operates exclusively on the fine-tuned weights. Existing methods apply a uniform merge across all tasks, ignoring the geometric relationships among their learned subspaces. When task updates occupy misaligned subspaces, projecting them onto a shared low-rank basis discards task-relevant directions, a failure mode named \emph{subspace interference}. Through this study, we show that the per-task projection error of a merged model is governed by the principal-angle alignment between each task and the shared subspace, so that grouping geometrically compatible tasks provably reduces this error within each group. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Group-wise Rank-Aware Model Merging (GRAM)}, which uses the principal-angle geometry of task vectors to decide which tasks should be merged together and then performs a standard SVD-based merge within each coalition; the pipeline requires only the fine-tuned weights at merge time. With only one additional model ($\nK{=}2$), GRAM significantly mitigates subspace interference and consistently outperforms prior merging methods across language understanding (GLUE with Flan-T5), 8-task CLIP vision, and medical instruction tuning (Qwen2-7B-Instruct with four English/Chinese medical LoRAs).

papers.title: Recursive Self-Improvement on a Budget: Scoring Code Edits Before They Run
papers.summary: A coding agent that rewrites its own scaffold has to choose which proposed edit to expand before that edit has been evaluated, and the search then has to return one agent. Each run fits one linear readout on the parent's steering-split solve rate and eight coordinates of the proposed diff, from 96 scaffold edits labeled by four evaluations of a 16-instance fit split, and then freezes the coefficients. HumanEval+ reserves 48 instances as the steering split and Polyglot reserves 64. That split scores parents and keeps an archive of four nodes. Huxley-Gödel Machine selection draws a parent by Thompson sampling on the steering counts of nodes that have already been evaluated, and it expands the child that parent proposes. Every method then returns the earliest evaluated node whose steering-split solve count is maximal. The tables report the held-out score of that node on the other 100 HumanEval+ instances and the other 145 Polyglot instances, next to the root scaffold and the calibration edit with the highest fit-split label. Twelve runs of GPT-4o return a node at 87.0% on held-out HumanEval+, against 84.2% for the parent-rate ablation. On that split Huxley-Gödel Machine selection returns 85.1%, the root is at 81.2%, and the calibration-best edit is at 82.8%. On the same split Claude Sonnet 4.5 returns 86.6%, beside 86.5% for Huxley-Gödel Machine selection, 85.3% for the parent-rate ablation, and 85.1% for the calibration-best edit.

papers.title: StochIKM: Automated High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Individual Patient Data from Published Kaplan-Meier Curves
papers.summary: Individual patient data are the gold standard for secondary analysis of time-to-event evidence, but they are rarely released, and reconstruction from a published Kaplan-Meier figure could help. Existing methods all claim high fidelity, each judged by whichever agreements it happens to achieve, and each returns a single dataset although the map from figure to data is not bijective. We define fidelity explicitly: a dataset is admissible when it reproduces the risk table exactly, follows the digitized curve to within the image resolution, and respects the printed median, interval and event count. We propose StochIKM, a stochastic algorithm that digitizes the figure with a vision-capable language model and uses the high-fidelity definition as constraints, returning an admissible set of individual patient datasets. A solution is guaranteed to exist whenever the figure has been read correctly, so a failure indicts either the published figure or its digitization. In simulation and in 79 arms from published oncology trials, StochIKM reproduces the published risk tables and medians more closely than LLM-improved IPDfromKM, a high-impact alternative.

papers.title: NormTune: Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Reasoning-Intensive Tasks
papers.summary: Full fine-tuning has achieved remarkable success on reasoning-intensive tasks, but it often requires substantial GPU resource consumption. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) provides a promising alternative for reducing this cost, yet we observe a substantial performance gap on reasoning-intensive tasks. In this paper, we present three key observations showing that this gap is closely associated with norm-related under-adaptation, where PEFT produces markedly smaller weight-update norms than full fine-tuning. Based on these observations, we propose Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (NormTune), a simple yet effective strategy that adaptively strengthens insufficiently updated layers according to their weight-update norms. Extensive experiments show that NormTune consistently enhances multiple PEFT methods across challenging reasoning benchmarks. Specifically, when trained on S1K-1.1, integrating NormTune into rank-8 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA yields substantial average accuracy improvements of 24.24\%, 11.33\%, and 16.21\% , respectively, across AIME 2024, MATH 500, GPQA, and AIME 2025. Moreover, NormTune-enhanced rank-256 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA achieve performance comparable to S1 full fine-tuning, with respective average gains of 2.17\%, 0.93\%, and 3.00\% over this baseline.

papers.title: LaVGuard: Selective Decoding for Contextual Value Drift
papers.summary: A content-safe response can still promote priorities that conflict with its task: an assistant may demand compliance when asked to preserve autonomy. We study contextual value drift as a task-relative decoding problem with an explicit allowance for change. LaVGuard separates an authorized ten-dimensional profile from a frozen estimate of the values expressed in the visible prefix. A profile-relative density gate selects when to evaluate candidate continuations; their signed progress determines a logit tilt constrained by both changed-position and cumulative-KL budgets. We establish local surrogate improvement, pathwise budget feasibility, and a bound on response-distribution change. Profile conditioning raises boundary TPR at 5% FPR from .58 to .72. At the same .12 mean intervention ratio, the selection study reports risk-safety scores of .88 for LaVGuard and .72 for position-matched edits. The resulting interface makes task priorities actionable while keeping the extent of intervention explicit and bounded.

papers.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
papers.summary: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.
papers.title_zh: 以陷阱预判世界模型引导黑盒大语言模型智能体
papers.abstract_zh: 前沿的黑盒大语言模型（LLM）智能体擅长长时程推理和精确动作生成。然而，当面对某个特定的智能体任务时，它们并不具备关于该特定环境如何展开的内化知识。世界模型提供了一种自然的补救办法，它通过预见环境将如何响应智能体即将采取的动作，为智能体提供特定于环境的知识。面向 LLM 智能体的已有世界模型主要预测每一步的下一观测，这种做法代价高昂且往往信息量不足，因为单个观测提供的任务相关指导有限，而且并非每一步都需要调用预见能力。这引出了一个关键问题：世界模型应该预测什么，以及在智能体任务中应在何时调用它？我们的初步研究表明，当世界模型在有界多步未来内预判陷阱时，其指导最为有用。受此启发，我们提出了陷阱预判世界模型（PAWM），它在潜在陷阱出现时选择性地进行干预，并预测即将发生的失败，以引导智能体避开该陷阱。PAWM 分两个阶段训练：首先在标注了智能体陷阱的合成数据上进行监督微调（SFT），随后与黑盒 LLM 进行 GRPO 协同训练，以在目标环境中进一步优化它。PAWM 在 ScienceWorld 上将 Claude Sonnet 4.5 的性能提升了 24.3%，在 WebArena-Lite 上提升了 7.7%，优于一系列基线。这些结果表明，PAWM 为黑盒 LLM 智能体提供了一种有效的世界模型指导形式。

papers.title: TeachBack: Learning to Teach via Bidirectional Preference Optimization for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables a language model to learn from a Teacher instantiated from the same model but given access to privileged information, such as a reference solution. We find that access to sufficient privileged information allows the Teacher to generate highly accurate trajectories; however, accuracy alone does not guarantee that these trajectories are suitable for Student learning. Direct access to a complete solution may encourage shortened, reference-conditioned derivations that omit the exploration, verification, and self-correction required to solve problems without privileged information. We introduce TeachBack, a bidirectional preference-learning framework for on-policy self-distillation that learns not only from the Teacher but also how the Teacher should teach. TeachBack shapes the Teacher's generation behavior by controlling the length of the reference-reasoning suffix injected into the prompt and by varying the prompt style. While maintaining comparable Teacher accuracy, it encourages the Teacher to explore and re-solve problems, thereby reducing its reliance on the reference solution. At each rollout refresh, the shared policy generates both a privileged Teacher trajectory and a problem-only Student trajectory. A pairwise preference objective uses privileged Teacher trajectories to improve Student learning, while the reversed preference uses the Student's behavior to shape future Teacher supervision under the privileged condition. Experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning tasks show that TeachBack consistently improves Student performance over existing OPSD methods and related baselines.

papers.title: When Multiple Choices Are Correct: Asymmetric Probability Allocation in Jev and Other Decision Models
papers.summary: Decision models return normalized probability distributions over candidate choices, which downstream applications can use to select among choices. Although their providers emphasize the reliability of these probabilities, calibration on tasks with a single correct choice does not establish their reliability when multiple choices are correct. We evaluate three decision models (Jev, Liquid d1, and GPT-6 Luna Decisions) on three diverse datasets (MetaTool, HotpotQA, and ECtHR) to study probability allocation and thresholding. Even when models rank every correct choice above every distractor, in 28% to 50% of those lists, at least one correct choice receives a probability below the uniform probability of 1/n, where n is the number of choices. We also present each model with five identical copies of a correct choice and observe probability disparities, with mean gaps ranging from 17 to 79 percentage points. We further show how these allocation disparities affect the recovery of multiple correct choices under probability thresholding. Decision-model probabilities can rank correct choices, but a probability threshold does not identify the set of correct choices.

papers.title: From Scores to Safe Sets: Exact Safety--Constrained Decoding for Medication Recommendation
papers.summary: Recent generative medication recommendation systems ultimately produce sets of drugs, but drug--drug interaction (DDI) constraints depend on the set as a whole. A natural post-hoc approach is to first predict medications and then locally repair interacting pairs by removing one drug at a time. We ask whether this local repair step itself introduces avoidable error. Using fixed medication scores from FLAME's frozen classifier on MIMIC-III, we compare increasingly strong local repair strategies with an exact global decoder while holding the scores, output size, and DDI constraint fixed. The global decoder jointly selects the highest-scoring feasible medication set using mixed-integer linear programming. Across validation and test splits, global decoding consistently achieves higher Jaccard similarity than greedy repair, degree-aware repair, and degree-aware repair strengthened with exhaustive 1-swap local search. Its advantage is small under loose DDI constraints and becomes larger as the constraint tightens; on the test split it reaches +0.0064 Jaccard over the strongest local baseline at the strict DDI operating point. The finding also holds across a fine accuracy--DDI sweep at matched realized DDI exposure and under three score representations. At the strict setting, global decoding retains more true-positive medications while removing more false positives. These results show that medication recommendation is not only a representation-learning problem: even with a frozen clinical model, how its scores are converted into a constrained medication set can materially affect the final prediction.

papers.title: CrashGym: Measuring the Decision Value of Experimentation for LLM Agents in Counterfactual Market Crashes
papers.summary: Language-model agents are increasingly asked to run experiments, yet benchmarks rarely measure whether those experiments improve the decisions they are meant to inform. We introduce CrashGym, a deterministic, replayable limit-order-book simulator in which an agent must choose between a deleveraging intervention and a liquidity backstop for a market about to suffer a shock-triggered crash. Before committing, the agent may query intervention experiments in a laboratory realization of the market. Its choice is then scored on an independently seeded target realization in which the simulator executes every feasible intervention, so regret relative to the best intervention is computed by directly simulating every alternative on the same target repeats, with no human or model-based judging. The simulator implements each amplification channel---persistent price impact, liquidity withdrawal, margin-driven liquidation, and an evolving strategy mix---as an explicit mechanism that can be switched on in stages. In a prospectively specified study on 24 newly sampled worlds, laboratory access reduces the mean regret of the one deployment with a complete record (Luna) from 8.878 to 3.785, a paired reduction of 5.092 utility units (nominal 95% world-bootstrap interval: 1.028--9.507), or 57.4% of the OBSERVE-ONLY mean. Prospective comparisons for two further deployments are incomplete; in a separate exploratory study, mean regret is lower with laboratory access for all four deployments evaluated. A laboratory whose strategy mix evolves endogenously yields no established advantage over one with a fixed mix. CrashGym thus measures the value of experimentation as avoided decision loss and lets simulator detail be judged by the decisions it supports.

papers.title: ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
papers.summary: Analogical reasoning is widely considered a fundamental component of human intelligence. Few benchmarks are designed to explicitly test far analogical reasoning - reasoning between domains that are superficially dissimilar yet share deep relational or structural similarities. In this work, we introduce an analogical reasoning benchmark called Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy (ARCANA). The tasks of ARCANA require performing far analogical mappings from real-world objects or physical phenomena to abstract grid-based transformations, different from the well-known ARC-AGI benchmark which primarily emphasized innate human priors. We validate ARCANA through a human study, demonstrating that humans solve these tasks reliably. In contrast, evaluations across a range of large language models show a distinct performance gap compared to humans, revealing systematic failure modes that remain challenging for current models. To address this gap, we propose ConceptSIR, a reasoning framework based on concept slippage, introspection, and reflection. Experiments demonstrate that ConceptSIR enables standard LLMs to solve several challenging ARCANA tasks that were unsolved by direct prompting in our evaluation. Overall, our results suggest that far analogical reasoning remains an open problem for contemporary LLMs. All the materials are available at sites.google.com/view/arcanacogtest. The complete codebase, including benchmark, and ConceptSIR, is publicly available at https://github.com/density-11/arcana-test. All ARCANA data and task instances can be accessed and explored at https://arcanacogtest.org/.
papers.title_zh: ARCANA：用于抽象与类比推理的基准
papers.abstract_zh: 类比推理被广泛认为是人类智能的一个基本组成部分。很少有基准被设计用来明确测试远类比推理——即在表面上不相似但在深层关系或结构上具有相似性的领域之间进行推理。在这项工作中，我们引入了一个名为“类比抽象与推理语料库”（Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy，ARCANA）的类比推理基准。ARCANA 的任务要求执行从现实世界对象或物理现象到抽象网格变换的远类比映射，这与主要强调人类先天先验的著名 ARC-AGI 基准不同。我们通过一项人类研究验证了 ARCANA，证明人类能够可靠地解决这些任务。相比之下，在一系列大语言模型上的评估显示出与人类相比明显的性能差距，揭示了当前模型仍然面临挑战的系统性失败模式。为弥补这一差距，我们提出了 ConceptSIR，一个基于概念滑移、内省和反思的推理框架。实验表明，ConceptSIR 使标准大语言模型能够解决若干在我们评估中通过直接提示未能解决的具有挑战性的 ARCANA 任务。总体而言，我们的结果表明，远类比推理仍然是当代大语言模型的一个开放问题。所有材料可在 sites.google.com/view/arcanacogtest 获取。完整代码库，包括基准和 ConceptSIR，已公开提供在 https://github.com/density-11/arcana-test。所有 ARCANA 数据和任务实例可在 https://arcanacogtest.org/ 访问和探索。

papers.title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support consequential decisions, yet their reliability under equivalent representations of uncertainty remains unclear. Existing work has documented prompt sensitivity, cognitive biases, and confidence miscalibration, but it is still unknown whether high-stakes advice changes when the same probability is expressed through complementary gain and loss frames. We introduce FrameBench-HPS, a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts derived from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education/career, and legal/consumer-rights domains. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing changes the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, with most changes involving uncertainty rather than direct reversals. Human evaluation confirms corresponding shifts in perceived risk and directiveness. Robustness experiments show that framing effects persist under conversational paraphrases and exceed ordinary repeated-generation variability. Probability canonicalization substantially reduces framing sensitivity, identifying probability representation as a practical target for improving consistency in high-stakes LLM decision support.
papers.title_zh: 相同概率，不同建议：高风险 LLM 决策支持中的收益-损失框架效应
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于支持会产生重大后果的决策，然而它们在不确定性的等价表示下的可靠性仍不清楚。现有工作已经记录了提示敏感性、认知偏差和置信度失准，但尚不清楚当同一概率通过互补的收益框架和损失框架表达时，高风险建议是否会发生变化。我们提出了 FrameBench-HPS，这是一个受控基准，包含 2,880 个提示，这些提示源自 240 个高风险场景，涵盖医疗保健、金融、教育/职业以及法律/消费者权益领域。在七个 LLM 中，收益-损失框架在 32.4% 的完整组中改变了建议类别，其中大多数变化涉及不确定性，而非直接反转。人工评估证实了感知风险和指导性方面存在相应变化。稳健性实验表明，框架效应在对话式改写下依然存在，并超过普通重复生成变异性。概率规范化大幅降低了框架敏感性，并将概率表示识别为改善高风险 LLM 决策支持一致性的一个实际目标。

papers.title: LLM-Based Exogenous World Modeling for Dynamic Scheduling
papers.summary: Dynamic scheduling requires dispatching online arrivals while anticipating future jobs, as poor decisions can compound downstream costs under nonlinear tardiness objectives. We show that a pretrained large language model (LLM) can serve as the exogenous component of a structured world model, forecasting uncertain future job arrivals. Specifically, we exploit an afterstate decomposition, which separates known deterministic shop transitions from uncertain exogenous job arrivals, enabling the LLM to forecast only the latter through a compact belief representation. Building on this, we develop Afterstate World-Model Planning (AWMP), which combines an evolved, belief-conditioned dispatching strategy with short scenario-based rollouts. A surprise-triggered refresh mechanism queries the LLM only when newly observed arrivals deviate sufficiently from previous forecast, and online residual self-calibration further conditions the LLM on its recent forecast errors to handle nonstationary arrivals. Across diverse arrival distributions, AWMP reduces weighted tardiness by 6-21% on dynamic job-shop and 22-46% on flexible job-shop benchmarks, relative to the best of eight classical priority-dispatching rules.
papers.title_zh: 基于大语言模型的外生世界建模用于动态调度
papers.abstract_zh: 动态调度需要在调度在线到达的同时预测未来作业，因为在非线性拖期目标下，糟糕的决策会叠加下游成本。我们表明，预训练大语言模型（LLM）可以作为结构化世界模型的外生组件，用于预测不确定的未来作业到达。具体而言，我们利用后状态分解，将已知的确定性车间状态转移与不确定的外生作业到达分离，使LLM仅通过紧凑的信念表示来预测后者。在此基础上，我们提出后状态世界模型规划（Afterstate World-Model Planning, AWMP），它将演化得到的、以信念为条件的派工策略与基于场景的短时推演相结合。一种由惊奇触发的刷新机制仅在新观测到的到达与先前预测偏离足够大时查询LLM，而在线残差自校准进一步使LLM以近期预测误差为条件，以处理非平稳到达。在不同的到达分布下，相对于八种经典优先派工规则中的最佳者，AWMP在动态作业车间基准上将加权拖期降低6-21%，在柔性作业车间基准上降低22-46%。

papers.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
papers.summary: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

papers.title: AgentMonopoly: Behavioral Patterns and Persona Control in LLM Agents
papers.summary: How do LLM agents' strategies differ, and how much can instructions to adopt a persona change their behavior over a game? We study these questions with AgentMonopoly, an environment where agents communicate, buy and trade properties, and make decisions that affect later turns. We compare models from four families, each at two sizes, in games with identical models, different sizes of the same family, or different families. We also assign one agent a persona, a description of how it should behave, intended to change a tendency observed in games without that persona. The tested models differ in how often they trade, waive rent, and manage cash and properties. Larger models do not consistently win more games. Persona instructions change the words agents use and some of their actions, but the changes do not always match the role across all decisions. These results show why persona following should be assessed through actions and outcomes as well as language. As our findings are conditional on the tested checkpoints, prompts, and five seeds per configuration, the open-source nature of AgentMonopoly provides the experimental infrastructure for further extending these comparisons. Our code is available at https://github.com/SuELS-Group/Agent_Monopoly.

papers.title: From Prompts to Posteriors: Can LLM Agents Perform Bayesian Inference in Context?
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied across the scientific discovery pipeline, from synthesizing literature to generating hypotheses to informing experimental design. A unifying principle behind these tasks is the need to continuously update beliefs as evidence accumulates, for which Bayesian inference provides a natural framework. However, existing work assumes that LLMs cannot carry out principled Bayesian belief updating in context, instead relying on simplifications and heuristics. To challenge this assumption, we present a principled evaluation of Bayesian reasoning capabilities in LLMs, analyzing both the model's internal consistency as well as its ability to recover an externally determined posterior. Specifically, we build an evaluation framework spanning qualitative epistemological examples to probe probabilistic coherence, quantitative benchmarks of Bayesian inference capabilities, and analyses of the impact of non-Bayesian updates on downstream task performance. Across different scenarios, we find that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule when updating their beliefs in context. However, when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution capabilities, their performance drastically improves, enabling even the close approximation of analytically intractable posteriors. Our evaluation shows that current LLMs with access to appropriate tools could already be used to make complex belief updates in scientific discovery, enabling rapid acceleration of the efficiency and scale of AI-powered scientific discovery.
papers.title_zh: 从提示到后验：LLM 智能体能否在上下文中执行贝叶斯推断？
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）正日益被应用于科学发现的整个流程，从综合文献到生成假设再到为实验设计提供依据。这些任务背后一个统一的原理是：随着证据的积累，需要不断更新信念，而贝叶斯推断为此提供了一个自然的框架。然而，已有工作假设 LLM 无法在上下文中进行有原则的贝叶斯信念更新，而是依赖于简化和启发式方法。为挑战这一假设，我们提出了一项对 LLM 中贝叶斯推理能力的有原则的评估，既分析模型的内部一致性，也分析其恢复由外部确定的后验分布的能力。具体而言，我们构建了一个评估框架，涵盖用于探究概率连贯性的定性认识论示例、贝叶斯推断能力的定量基准，以及对非贝叶斯更新对下游任务性能影响的分析。在不同场景中，我们发现 LLM 在上下文中更新其信念时通常会违反贝叶斯法则。然而，当配备现代推理能力和代码执行能力时，它们的表现会大幅提升，甚至能够对解析上难以处理的后验分布进行接近的近似。我们的评估表明，当前具备适当工具访问权限的 LLM 已经可以被用于在科学发现中进行复杂的信念更新，从而快速加速 AI 驱动的科学发现在效率和规模上的提升。

papers.title: Solving Go under Positional Superko: Sound Proof Transfer and New Board Values
papers.summary: Positional superko (PSK) forbids recreating any earlier whole-board position. It is part of the Chinese rules as written and of the rules used in computer Go. Yet almost all solved Go boards were computed under a simpler basic-ko rule set. PSK makes solving hard: legality depends on the whole game history, and this breaks the three tools that make solving tractable, namely transposition tables (the graph-history interaction problem), static life-and-death recognition, and safe move pruning. We present Sanko, a parallel depth-first proof-number solver that restores all three soundly. Its core is a cheap proof-transfer theorem: a stored proof stays valid on a new path unless a board that the proof's winner must create has already occurred. Sanko proves 5x5 Go in 16 minutes with six threads, where the previous state of the art needed 5.25 hours with six processes, and in about a minute and a half on one 192-thread machine. It also establishes the first PSK values of twenty-three further boards, eleven of which were unsolved under any rules. Superko changes game-theoretic values: 4x7, a full-board win under basic ko, is worth only 12 points under PSK, and we pinpoint the move at which the previously published optimal line fails. Unlike earlier solutions of empty Go boards, we release the solver source together with the command line and outcome of every run behind our values and measurements, so that all reported values can be reproduced.

papers.title: MERP: A Latent-Bottleneck Framework for Robust Multi-Modal Multi-Label Emotion Recognition
papers.summary: Multimodal multi-label emotion recognition is important for affect-aware systems, but models trained with complete text, visual, and acoustic streams often degrade sharply when some streams are unavailable at deployment. We address this train-test gap by learning a compact representation that preserves emotion-specific evidence from any available subset of modalities. We propose the Multi-modal Emotion Recognition Perceiver (MERP), which maps the joint sequence into a fixed-size latent bank, thereby keeping repeated reasoning independent of raw input length; it extracts label-specific evidence before and after latent reasoning and aligns the two levels through reconstruction. MERP further uses positive and negative class prototypes, a noise-gated feature enhancer with frequency-shaped perturbations during training, and confidence-aware class-wise fusion to strengthen separability, reduce sensitivity to missing inputs, and combine complementary predictors. Under 20 percent test-time random modality drop, MERP achieves micro-F1 scores of 0.563 on CMU-MOSEI and 0.780 on M3ED, exceeding the strongest evaluated baselines by 0.004 and 0.005, respectively; in the severe CMU-MOSEI audio-only setting, it retains 0.473 micro-F1 versus 0.022 for LDDU. These results show that fixed latent reasoning provides a practical, testable route to robust multimodal emotion recognition without requiring missing-modality examples during training. Code is available at https://github.com/Creative-zcx/MERP.

papers.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
papers.summary: World models are increasingly used for planning, where a planner ranks candidate actions by returns imagined by the model. However, these models are judged mainly by how well they render frames, even though a visually faithful rollout can still assign the wrong return. To identify where this mismatch arises, we introduce a transition-level diagnostic that replaces imagined transitions with real ones and measures the reduction in return error against a budget-matched random control. Our analysis yields two findings. (1) Event transitions, the few steps where a reward is earned or an episode ends, are rendered as well as other steps (median pixel-error ratio 0.85), yet restoring them removes a median of 70% of the return error. In contrast, restoring transitions with the largest MSE, SSIM or LPIPS error removes less than a random choice. Across the 44 Atari-100k model--collection pairs that pass our reliability checks, including three released families, event patches outperform random patches in 39 (sign test p=1.4 x 10^{-7}), with a median gain of +44 percentage points. (2) The remaining error is structured: a complementary patch separates errors at true events from those elsewhere, while an eight-step timing tolerance recovers few events missed by our deterministic models. This structure also guides repair: a rule recorded before four repair outcomes were known predicts when a diffusion model repairs these failures. Event patches improve plan ranking, and the same concentration appears on control tasks with rare reward events.
papers.title_zh: 事件，而非像素：世界模型在何处把回报弄错
papers.abstract_zh: 世界模型越来越多地用于规划，其中规划器根据模型想象出的回报对候选动作进行排序。然而，这些模型主要根据其渲染帧的效果来评判，尽管视觉上忠实的展开轨迹仍可能赋予错误的回报。为识别这种不匹配在何处产生，我们引入一种转移级诊断方法，它用真实转移替换想象转移，并相对于预算匹配的随机对照来测量回报误差的降低。我们的分析得出两点发现。（1）事件转移，即获得奖励或回合结束的少数步骤，其渲染得与其他步骤一样好（像素误差中位比率为 0.85），然而恢复它们可在中位数上消除 70% 的回报误差。相比之下，恢复具有最大 MSE、SSIM 或 LPIPS 误差的转移所消除的误差少于随机选择。在通过我们可靠性检查的 44 个 Atari-100k 模型—集合对中，包括三个已发布的家族，事件补丁在 39 个中优于随机补丁（符号检验 p=1.4 x 10\^{-7}），中位增益为 +44 个百分点。（2）剩余误差是有结构的：一个互补补丁将真实事件处的误差与其他位置的误差区分开，而八步的时间容差仅能恢复我们的确定性模型漏掉的少数事件。这种结构也指导修复：一条在四个修复结果已知之前记录的规则，预测扩散模型何时修复这些失败。事件补丁改善了计划排序，并且同样的集中现象也出现在奖励事件稀疏的控制任务上。

papers.title: PreCoMem: Predictive Cognitive Memory for Self-Evolving Long-Term Dialogue Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon dialogue agents need to keep user memories stable enough for personalization while adapting when the user genuinely changes. Existing memory systems often append every observation or overwrite old entries by heuristic rules, which makes transient noise hard to distinguish from real belief drift. We introduce PreCoMem, a memory consolidation framework inspired by predictive coding that represents memory as confidence-weighted beliefs about the user's state. Its core signal, Effective Surprisal, combines semantic deviation and contradiction evidence, then downweights this signal when retrieval is diffuse and unreliable.
