Separately, ArXiv four-concept composition improves over an averaged-direction comparator after independent validation gates and first-use test evaluation.

papers.title: Beyond Binary Labels: Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Safety with Prompt-Level Rubrics
papers.summary: Current LLM safety benchmarks predominantly rely on binary safe or unsafe labels, lacking explanatory depth and suffering from low consistency across automated judges. To address this, we introduce DiagSafe, a diagnostic evaluation framework that moves beyond binary classification by employing prompt-level rubrics. Grounded in globally applicable AI safety policies, each rubric provides explicit criteria along two dimensions: safety, which targets concrete harms with specific exemptions to suppress false positives, and usefulness, which independently evaluates instruction fulfillment. To ensure a robust and realistic evaluation, we construct a bilingual (English-Chinese) benchmark grounded in a comprehensive 84-label safety taxonomy, consisting of two subsets: DiagBase, which covers single- and multi-turn prompts with direct harmful queries and template-based jailbreaks, and DiagAttack, which embeds harmful intents into complex instruction-following tasks to form challenging instruction attacks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DiagSafe significantly enhances the reliability of LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, achieving 95.34% agreement with human annotations -- substantially higher than the 69%-87% achieved by the baselines -- and high inter-judge consistency (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.864). Furthermore, applying our framework reveals that leading LLMs differ markedly in their unsafe rates, and each model also exhibits unique vulnerabilities along different dimensions. In addition, we observe that models are particularly susceptible in Chinese and multi-turn contexts. Ultimately, DiagSafe provides a reliable and explainable tool for auditing and optimizing LLM alignment.

papers.title: MOSAIC: An Omni-Modal Benchmark for Long-Term Memory and Cross-Modal Reasoning in Conversational Agents
papers.summary: Omni-modal assistants must remember not only what users say, but also what they show and convey. Existing long-term memory benchmarks are mostly text-and-image or report a single end-to-end score, so they cannot locate whether evidence is lost when it is represented, retrieved, delivered, or read. We introduce MOSAIC, a benchmark of 923 questions over persona-grounded histories of 11-24 sessions spanning text, image, video, and audio. MOSAIC constructs targeted spatial, temporal, and prosodic signals rather than decorative media, with the strongest causal validation for spatial information and selector-level validation for annotated prosody, and pairs them with a matched diagnostic protocol that freezes the question, reader, prompt, and budget while intervening on representation, retrieval, and delivery. Matched decomposition shows that representation loss is modality-dependent, residual reading dominates even under gold evidence, and abstention remains weak on these controls: strong answerable scores coexist with failures to refuse. MOSAIC thus turns omni-modal memory evaluation from a leaderboard into a diagnosis of write, retrieve, deliver, and read failures.

papers.title: Let Agents Design How They Search: Automatic Interface Optimization for Agentic Search
papers.summary: Agentic search depends on the interface through which a language-model agent accesses and explores a corpus. Existing interface designs are fixed by hand and applied unchanged to every corpus, although effective designs may depend on the corpus. We introduce SearchWeaver, a framework for automatic search interface optimization guided by downstream search performance. A proposer uses execution trajectories and task rewards to jointly revise corpus artifacts, executable tools, and usage instructions. This pro cess optimizes what information is prepared in advance, which operations tools perform, and which decisions remain with the search agent. With GPT-5.4-nano, the optimized interfaces improve answer accuracy from 71.6% to 78.4% on BrowseComp-Plus and average nDCG@10 from 45.7 to 55.0 across four BRIGHT subsets over Direct Corpus Interaction. These findings highlight the value of jointly optimizing corpus artifacts, executable tools, and usage instructions to develop effective search interfaces.

papers.title: Intergroup Bias Predicts Expressions of Social Judgment and Empathy in the r/AmITheAsshole Reddit Community
papers.summary: People share and understand others' experiences differently based on their social identities; often, people empathize more when the other person belongs to their ingroup compared to an outgroup. While this intergroup empathy gap is well-studied in social psychology, it remains unclear how it manifests in naturally occurring online social interactions. To this end, we measure how commenters express social judgments, as an indirect outcome of their understanding towards the posters, and empathy in text, based on whether commenters share the poster's gender or are of similar ages. We focus on posts where the poster self-reports these demographics, and analyze 126,716 comments associated with 36,163 posts from 18,111 commenters in r/AmItheAsshole, while controlling for commenter and poster group identities, post features (topic, length, and score), and both commenter- and post-level variance. Our results show that when commenters and posters are ingroup, in either gender or age, commenters are more likely to provide a Not the Asshole verdict and show greater text-based understanding as measured by LLMs. We also observe that older commenters behave differently from younger ones. Furthermore, in a subset of posts where the gender and age of the other party in the conflict are explicitly mentioned, we find that commenter-poster ingroup effects are moderated by the group relationships between the poster and the other party when commenters make social judgments. Our work highlights the importance of intergroup context and social group nuances in understanding online discourse.

papers.title: Hierarchical Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.summary: Masked diffusion language models have emerged as an alternative to autoregressive models, enabling parallel token generation. However, standard masked diffusion language models use a shared noise schedule across positions without explicitly encoding which positions should be resolved first. Many tasks exhibit a natural priority among positions: document titles and section headings can guide the generation of body text, while Sudoku cells determined directly from the initial clues can help resolve more difficult cells. To incorporate this notion of priority (or hierarchy) among token positions, we introduce the Hierarchical Masked Diffusion Language Model (HMDLM), which augments each token position with a hierarchy level available as part of the training data, and requires zero or minimal additional annotations. It factors generation into two passes: the first predicts a hierarchy distribution over masked positions, the second predicts token distributions conditioned on it. Giving each hierarchy level its own noise schedule induces a soft, controllable preference for revealing higher-priority positions earlier while keeping decoding fully parallel. Our formulation is mathematically grounded, and we re-derive the forward and reverse processes and the NELBO for this factorization. Our evaluation shows that for the task of language generation on LM1B, HMDLM reduces perplexity by more than 1.5 points over Anchored Diffusion Language Model (ADLM), a recently proposed strong diffusion baseline; on WikiHow, we see a drop in perplexity of up to 4.4 pts on ADLM and up to 7 pts against MDLM. An LLM judge on WikiHow prefers HMDLM generations (the two variants combined) more than $2\times$ as often as the baseline. On the task of solving Sudoku puzzles requiring multi-step reasoning, it improves solution accuracy by up to $8.6\%$ absolute points over existing diffusion baselines.
papers.title_zh: 分层掩码扩散语言模型
papers.abstract_zh: 掩码扩散语言模型已成为自回归模型的一种替代方案，能够实现并行 token 生成。然而，标准掩码扩散语言模型在各位置上使用共享的噪声调度，而没有显式编码哪些位置应首先被解析。许多任务在位置之间表现出自然的优先级：文档标题和章节标题可以指导正文文本的生成，而可直接由初始线索确定的数独单元格有助于解析更困难的单元格。为了在 token 位置之间引入这种优先级（或层级）概念，我们提出分层掩码扩散语言模型（HMDLM），它使用作为训练数据一部分可用的层级级别来增强每个 token 位置，并且需要零或极少量的额外标注。它将生成分解为两遍：第一遍预测掩码位置上的层级分布，第二遍以该分布为条件预测 token 分布。为每个层级赋予其自身的噪声调度，会诱导一种柔和且可控的偏好，即更早揭示更高优先级的位置，同时保持解码完全并行。我们的表述具有数学依据，并且我们针对该分解重新推导了前向过程、反向过程以及 NELBO。我们的评估表明，在 LM1B 上的语言生成任务中，HMDLM 相比 Anchored Diffusion Language Model (ADLM)——一个最近提出的强扩散基线——将困惑度降低超过 1.5 点；在 WikiHow 上，我们看到相对于 ADLM 的困惑度最多下降 4.4 点，相对于 MDLM 最多下降 7 点。在 WikiHow 上，一个 LLM 评判器偏好 HMDLM 生成结果（两个变体合并）的频率超过基线的 $2\times$。在需要多步推理的数独谜题求解任务上，它相比现有扩散基线将求解准确率最多提高 $8.6\%$ 绝对百分点。

papers.title: Credit Where Credit Is Due: Contrastive Attribution Topology Search for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: An LLM multi-agent system (MAS) is only as good as the agents it chooses to trust: its accuracy and cost hinge on its topology, meaning which agents are included and how they communicate. A single task score, however, does not reveal which agents help or hinder performance. We propose Contrastive Attribution Topology Search (CATS), which searches for compact teams within a fixed supergraph of specialized agents. An LLM attributer compares execution traces across candidate topologies and assigns credit to individual agents. CATS uses these credits to update supergraph edges while progressively pruning weak edges and agents, yielding a small team for deployment. With small open-weight models and matched candidate evaluations, CATS improves mean accuracy on BigCodeBench by 5.3 percentage points over score-only heuristic search while using 54\% fewer deployment tokens. On MBPP, CATS matches the strongest baselines with fewer tokens than the other searches. In a HotpotQA prompt-poisoning stress test, CATS excludes all adversarially prompted agents in all three runs, whereas random search retains some at comparable accuracy. Per-agent credit thus supports both team optimization and the pruning of potentially harmful agents.

papers.title: Asking What a Director Sees Can Change What Vision-Language Models Choose
papers.summary: Vision-language models are now routinely tested on theory of mind: whether they can work out what another person sees, knows, and means. A common design asks the model to report that perspective and then to act for the person, and reads a correct report beside a wrong action as a failure to use the perspective. That reading rests on a quiet assumption: that asking for the report leaves the action unchanged. We show that it does not. In a rendered Director Task, a partition hides the largest block from a director who asks for "the largest block". Asking first which blocks the director can see raises the share of replies that choose this hidden block by 12 to 88 percentage points on six GPT models and by 17 on Qwen3.8-27B, even though the models mostly report correctly which blocks the director sees. Reasoning traces and prompt rewordings suggest why: the question shifts how the request is read, from the director's view toward the model's own. When the prompt states what the director knows and refers to, fewer than 1% of replies pair a correct report with a hidden-block choice. Any evaluation that elicits a perspective report before the action it scores needs a baseline without the question, and we deliver one: paired prompts that differ only in that question, a design any perspective-taking benchmark can adopt.

papers.title: OSynth: A Longitudinal, Context-Sensitive Evaluation of Meeting Understanding
papers.summary: Meeting notetakers are increasingly deployed in settings where longitudinal context is available including calendar metadata, prior meetings, emails, slides, and speaker enrollments; however, meeting corpora remain limited in terms of size, domain coverage, and available context. We present OSynth, a large-scale synthetic dataset of simulated organizations comprising 570 hours of meeting audio together with associated artifacts and a latent ground-truth state. In a pairwise comparison, human raters distinguish OSynth meetings from real meeting transcripts with only 56% accuracy based on excerpts of 150-300 words. Across state-of-the-art LLMs, additional context yields significant gains on several entity-sensitive dimensions, demonstrating limitations of contemporary approaches and the potential usefulness of OSynth in developing better-contextualized meeting-understanding systems.

papers.title: Signals and Queries: Token-Efficient Agentic Context Discovery
papers.summary: User-facing LLM agents must identify which behavioral policies apply at each turn, but evaluating every policy with an LLM is costly. We introduce Signals and Queries (S&Q), a lightweight first-stage relevance filter developed for Parlant 4.0 that removes at least 30% of candidate policies before downstream evaluation while preserving high recall. For each policy, an LLM generates activating examples and hard negatives offline. An independent logistic classifier trained on their embeddings then predicts relevance using embeddings and vector dot products, with no per-turn LLM calls. This shifts expensive relevance evaluation to a smaller candidate set, while allowing each policy's classifier to be updated independently. Evaluated against 9,144 LLM-judge relevance labels covering 254 $τ^2$-bench conversation prefixes and 36 airline policies, S&Q achieves higher precision than top-K and cosine-threshold retrieval at every evaluated recall level, with consistent results across two embedding providers. These findings support inexpensive, per-policy classification as a practical first stage for reducing downstream evaluation workload in customer-facing agents.

papers.title: Seeing the Forest for the Trees: Emergent Agreement from Individual Conversations
papers.summary: As LLM agents interact in the wild and shape each other's decisions, understanding how they converge toward agreement becomes important. We study this in multi-turn conversations where two LLMs discuss subjective matters, can agree or disagree, and may change their stances. Using a linear classifier on individual conversation activations, we identify an internal representation of agreement. We find that it varies substantially across turns and conversations and does not reliably track external agreement at the individual conversation level. We therefore move beyond the representation of agreement in individual conversations, by aggregating the agreement representation across conversations. Externally, this aggregate view reveals a simple structure: when pooled across conversations, agreement can be predicted well with a Markov process, with agreement at each turn being a direct function of agreement at the previous turn. Similarly, when internal agreement is aggregated, it couples with the external Markov agreement through a power-law mapping, exposing Markovian dynamics in internal representations. Additionally, we find that after a change of stance, models express agreement externally before their internal representations reflect the same shift. These results reveal a joint structure between internal and external agreement that emerges only when internal features are aggregated across conversations. Code available at https://github.com/technion-cs-nlp/SeeingTheForestForTheTrees.

papers.title: Policy Central: Detecting Conflicts, Redundancy, and Similarity in Deployed Police Policy
papers.summary: Policy Central is a deployed system that helps police departments find relationships between sections of their written policy: whether two sections conflict, are redundant, are merely similar, or are different. We describe the system and compare two architectures. Retrieve-Judge, a retrieve-then-classify pipeline, runs as a cheap library-wide health signal; Screen-Confirm, a screen-then-confirm cascade, is a selective audit of the documents a reviewer chooses, checking them exhaustively against one another. On a 302-pair benchmark drawn from one department's ~84 real policy documents, given each pair Screen-Confirm reaches 0.795 aggregate recall and 0.885 on Conflict, so current models judge well. Finding the pair is the hard part: Retrieve-Judge's composed recall falls to 0.457, and Screen-Confirm recovers 0.472 (0.615 on Conflict). Today these pairs are found by reading the whole library, nearly 20,000 sections, checked against one another and re-checked after every revision. A scan that returns half of them in minutes, at low cost, and can be re-run on demand changes the economics of policy review even before recall improves.

papers.title: ChronoSynth: Constraint-Aware Question Synthesis over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
papers.summary: Knowledge graph question generation (KGQG) generates natural-language questions from structured graph evidence and a target answer. When the input graph is temporal, a valid question must also preserve the answer field, time condition, reference event, and temporal order that determine the answer set. Existing KGQG methods and prompting baselines can produce fluent questions that alter these conditions, causing temporal semantic drift. This paper studies temporal KGQG as a constraint-preserving graph-to-question problem and proposes ChronoSynth, a memory-augmented and constraint-aware generation framework. ChronoSynth first constructs a Temporal Intent State to make the intended question semantics explicit. It then retrieves compatible typed question patterns from an indexed pattern memory, adapts them to the input graph, and validates the generated question. Validation feedback guides revisions when a supported inconsistency is detected. Experiments on CRONQUESTIONS and MultiTQ demonstrate state-of-the-art generation performance, with ablations supporting the contributions of its components.

papers.title: B-CARE: Blind Classwise Assessment of Relative Evidence for Stance Error Ranking
papers.summary: Stance classifiers make errors that can be costly to identify under limited human-review budgets. Prioritizing potentially incorrect predictions remains challenging, particularly across heterogeneous base models. We introduce B-CARE (Blind Classwise Assessment of Relative Evidence for Stance Error Ranking), a prediction-blind framework for identifying high-risk stance predictions. Given only a target and text, a fixed LLM verifier assigns ordinal evidence scores to all candidate stance labels without observing the base model's prediction or confidence. B-CARE constructs a comparative risk score by contrasting the strongest alternative-class evidence with the evidence supporting the predicted class. The resulting classwise evidence profile can be reused across multiple base models without training a separate error detector or calibrating risk scores. We evaluate B-CARE on four stance benchmarks and three heterogeneous base LLMs, covering 12 dataset-model settings and 5,206 unique test instances. Evaluation includes error-ranking discrimination (AUROC and AUPRC), selective prediction (E-AURC), and review effectiveness (ErrorCapture at fixed review budgets). B-CARE achieves a mean AUROC of 0.735 and a mean AUPRC of 0.524, capturing 41.06% of errors within the highest-risk 20% of predictions. Although B-CARE does not uniformly outperform strong confidence-based baselines, it provides a reusable, complementary evidence signal for prioritizing potentially incorrect stance predictions across heterogeneous models.

papers.title: Don't Stop Long-Context Continual Pre-Training Too Early: An Empirical Scaling Law
papers.summary: Long-context continual pre-training (LCCP) is widely used to improve long-context capability, but how its benefits scale with the number of tokens used for LCCP remains unclear. We investigate this question through modeling, monitoring, and validating the benefits of scaling LCCP. First, we establish an empirical additive power law relating long-context performance to model size and the respective token budgets of short-context pre-training and LCCP. Experiments across five model scales and more than one hundred short- and long-context budget configurations show that the fitted law reproduces the observed trends and extrapolates well to held-out model scales. Second, we introduce \textsc{Constant-Last4}, a training and observation protocol that averages the four most recent consecutive checkpoints from a constant-learning-rate run to enable stable monitoring along a single extensible training trajectory. Under this protocol, the same scaling-law form fits well and accurately predicts the LCCP performance trajectory of a 1.22B-parameter model trained on approximately 100B LCCP tokens. Finally, downstream evaluations along this trajectory show continued improvements in long-context performance, with no clear sign of saturation within the evaluated range. These gains persist after both 128K context extension and supervised fine-tuning, with benefits extending to long-context understanding and agentic tasks. Together, these results argue for continuing to scale LCCP rather than stopping early: its gains are stably observable along an extensible trajectory, quantitatively predictable, and transferable to downstream tasks.

papers.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
papers.summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. Whether memory can drive genuine continual learning remains an open question. In this paper, we introduce Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL), arguing that memory should be judged by whether it improves future actions, not merely what it retrieves. MCCL has three main parts. First, a three-axis taxonomy organizes memory by where state is stored (substrates), what form it takes (assets), and how it is managed (policies). This defines a two-loop lifecycle that updates memory state in an inner loop while refining management policies in an outer loop based on task feedback. Second, an evaluation protocol measures retention under interference, adaptation to change, and task transfer to isolate genuine behavioral gains from simple context expansion. Third, a memory scaling framework models how agent performance scales with experience, storage capacity, and compute budgets across non-parametric and parametric memory. Together, these components reframe agent memory from passive lookup to continuous learning, offering a principled route toward self-improving autonomous agents.

papers.title: Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories
papers.summary: Quantization-aware training (QAT) aims to recover reasoning capabilities in low-bit large language models (LLMs). Existing recipes typically supervise the quantized student with the original full-precision model on fixed response sequences. However, the resulting low-bit quantized models still struggle on long-horizon reasoning tasks and often fail to terminate within a token budget that suffices for the full-precision model. We identify two challenges in closing this gap. First, fixed-response supervision leaves a mismatch between training prefixes and those encountered during student generation, and this trajectory divergence grows as responses lengthen. Second, on its own prefixes, the student underpredicts some next-token candidates and overpredicts others, and this distributional misalignment becomes more frequent at high-entropy prefixes. We present OnQ, a low-bit recovery pipeline that combines on-policy distillation and candidate-wise Dynamic KL. Starting from block-wise calibration, the quantized student generates responses and receives full-precision teacher supervision on its own prefixes. Dynamic KL weights forward and reverse KL by each candidate's teacher-student probability ratio to balance correction of under- and overprediction. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at 2- and 3-bit precision, OnQ achieves the highest nine-benchmark average, with the largest gains on long-horizon reasoning benchmarks. At 2 bits, it outperforms every baseline on every benchmark at every model size, improving the Qwen3-8B average by 10.26 points over the strongest baseline. It also produces shorter responses with fewer truncations and repetitive errors.
papers.title_zh: Right On Q：通过自生成轨迹在量化条件下恢复推理能力
papers.abstract_zh: 量化感知训练（QAT）旨在恢复低比特大语言模型（LLM）的推理能力。现有方案通常在固定响应序列上，用原始全精度模型监督量化学生模型。然而，所得低比特量化模型在长时程推理任务上仍然表现不佳，并且常常无法在足以让全精度模型完成任务的 token 预算内终止。我们指出了缩小这一差距所面临的两个挑战。第一，固定响应监督会造成训练前缀与学生生成过程中遇到的前缀之间的不匹配，而且这种轨迹偏差会随着响应变长而增大。第二，在学生模型自身的前缀上，它会对某些下一 token 候选预测不足，而对另一些候选预测过度，并且这种分布失配在高熵前缀处会更加频繁。我们提出 OnQ，一种结合同策略蒸馏与逐候选 Dynamic KL 的低比特恢复流程。从逐块校准开始，量化学生模型生成响应，并在其自身前缀上接受全精度教师的监督。Dynamic KL 根据每个候选的教师-学生概率比来对前向 KL 和反向 KL 进行加权，以平衡对预测不足和预测过度的校正。在 2 比特和 3 比特精度下的 Qwen3-1.7B、4B 和 8B 上，OnQ 取得了最高的九项基准平均成绩，并在长时程推理基准上取得最大增益。在 2 比特下，它在每个模型规模的每个基准上都优于所有基线，将 Qwen3-8B 的平均成绩相较最强基线提高了 10.26 分。它还能生成更短的响应，且截断和重复错误更少。

papers.title: ECHO: Emergent Common-Mode Hidden Offsets Drive Vocabulary Collapse in Preference Optimization
papers.summary: Preference optimization can improve every ranking metric while building a hidden, shared representation shift that the relative loss barely sees, one that can eventually destroy generation. We trace this failure to the common-mode offset, a shared directional shift in the model's hidden states that appears across token positions, prompts, and both chosen and rejected responses. Because it moves chosen and rejected representations together, the relative ranking loss barely reacts to its accumulation. As this offset grows, it projects onto the output layer to form a vocabulary well, elevating a single token's probability until it dominates decoding and causes generation collapse. The isolated offset alone reconstructs the vocabulary well, injecting the learned offset into an untreated base model recreates the collapse where norm-matched random directions do not, and masking this common component from the loss prevents the well in our flagship setting. Under the per-token ranking loss we study, the same collapse appears in 14 of 17 base-model lineages and under full-parameter fine-tuning. Moreover, the offset is not merely an artifact of collapse, since it is already present in textbook DPO and SimPO runs that form no well. Textbook DPO keeps it weakly aligned with any single vocabulary direction even with three times our base budget. Trained from base models for that budget, however, full-parameter SimPO drives it into collapse on both Llama-2 and Llama-3.1, and the same kind of offset grows, without a well, from a public SFT checkpoint under the official SimPO recipe. Across 17 UltraFeedback runs, the better a run ranks held-out responses, the less often two public reward models prefer its samples to the base model's. These findings expose a blind spot in standard ranking metrics and introduce a representation-level signal that can warn of generation collapse before it occurs.

papers.title: Beyond Small Talk: Modeling Disclosure Trajectories in Human-AI Conversation
papers.summary: Recently, we see a rise in conversational agents as a form of social and emotional support, where disclosure will unfold over time. Yet, current evaluations of these agents typically examine isolated conversational states. In analyses of naturally occurring conversations, disclosure history and current disclosure are confounded which tends to make their effects difficult to isolate. We thus introduce Trajectory-based Disclosure Evaluation (TraDE), an evaluation framework grounded in Social Penetration Theory that utilizes predefined disclosure trajectories and evaluates how preceding disclosure history shapes model behavior under matched current disclosure. Through the use of TraDE, we demonstrate across multiple models and relational behavior benchmarks that responses to disclosures matched on depth can differ depending on the preceding trajectory, particularly in whether models accept or challenge the user's framing. We also observed that these differences track accumulated exposure to deeper disclosure rather than any single moment of vulnerability or the order of disclosures. It also tends to persists for several turns after disclosure returns to shallow levels. For several behaviors, we also demonstrate that models diverge most consistently from human supporters in the Emotional Support Conversation corpus (ESConv) not when users open up but rather when they step back in their disclosure. TraDE thus provides a systematic way to expose history-dependent relational behavior that evaluations of isolated conversational states would otherwise miss.

papers.title: A KAN-based Non-linear Factorization for Embedding Layer Compression
papers.summary: Among existing embedding compression approaches, low-rank factorization provides a simple and mathematically principled solution by approximating the embedding matrix with a reduced-rank decomposition. However, its practical effectiveness is often limited, as the resulting linear bottleneck constrains representational capacity. To overcome these limitations, we propose an enhanced factorization scheme that increases expressive power by introducing learnable non-linear projections within the compressed embedding layer. Our method is inspired by the Kolmogorov Arnold Networks (KAN) paradigm, which replaces fixed linear transformations with learnable univariate functions. Despite promising results in other domains, applications of KANs in NLP remain scarce and have so far been largely limited to final or task specific layers, rather than core representational components such as embedding layers. We evaluate the proposed approach by integrating the compressed embedding layer into the Skip-gram framework and comparing it against a standard low-rank baseline under matched parameter budgets on the Word Analogy and Semantic Similarity benchmarks. We further introduce an effective initialization strategy from a pre-trained, uncompressed embedding layer. The behavior of the model is analyzed both immediately after initialization and after a brief post-initialization refinement phase, considering training with the standard Skip-gram objective as well as variants augmented with distillation from the original embedding layer. Overall, our results show that augmenting low-rank factorization with learnable non-linear projections effectively mitigates the limitations of linear bottlenecks, yielding more faithful compressed embeddings under fixed dimensionality and suggesting a promising direction for embedding layer compression beyond purely linear methods.

papers.title: DynaWeave: Learning to Adapt through Dynamic Scenario Synthesis
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use tools to complete tasks in stateful environments. However, many training environments remain largely static apart from changes caused by the agent's own actions, whereas external events introduced by other users, services, or sudden contingencies in real environments can invalidate ongoing plans. To address this gap, we introduce DynaWeave, an automated synthesis framework that transforms existing static tasks into verifiable dynamic scenarios. The framework generates exogenous events relevant to each task, covering changes in task requirements, environment state, and external information. It uses directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to represent dependencies between events and an execution engine to activate them during agent interaction. A dynamic verifier revises only the evaluation checks affected by events that actually occur and retains all other checks. Using DynaWeave, we collect 2,095 verified interaction trajectories across 36 environments and use them for supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5 models. Experiments on Gaia2, CostBench, and ToolMaze show that DynaWeave achieves consistent improvements in overall performance across all three evaluated model sizes, increasing the task completion rate on CostBench by 67.34 percentage points and even exceeding the performance of Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview on ToolMaze. These results support dynamic scenario synthesis as a practical approach to training agents to adapt to changing environments. Our code is available at https://github.com/Miaow-Lab/DynaWeave.
papers.title_zh: DynaWeave：通过动态场景合成学习适应
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地使用工具在有状态环境中完成任务。然而，除了智能体自身动作所引起的变化之外，许多训练环境在很大程度上仍是静态的，而真实环境中由其他用户、服务或突发意外引入的外部事件会使正在进行的计划失效。为弥补这一差距，我们提出了 DynaWeave，一个自动化合成框架，可将现有静态任务转化为可验证的动态场景。该框架生成与每个任务相关的外生事件，涵盖任务需求、环境状态和外部信息的变化。它使用有向无环图（DAGs）表示事件之间的依赖关系，并使用执行引擎在智能体交互期间激活这些事件。动态验证器仅修改受实际发生事件影响的评估检查，并保留所有其他检查。使用 DynaWeave，我们在 36 个环境中收集了 2,095 条已验证的交互轨迹，并将其用于对 Qwen3.5 模型进行监督微调。在 Gaia2、CostBench 和 ToolMaze 上的实验表明，DynaWeave 在所有三种被评估的模型规模上均在整体性能上取得了一致提升，将 CostBench 上的任务完成率提高了 67.34 个百分点，甚至在 ToolMaze 上超过了 Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview 的性能。这些结果支持将动态场景合成作为一种训练智能体适应不断变化环境的实用方法。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/Miaow-Lab/DynaWeave 获取。

papers.title: Omnilingual-MsASR: Benchmarking Multimodal, Multilingual, Long-Form Multi-Speaker ASR of Omni Large Language Models
papers.summary: Omni-modal large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in audio and video understanding. However, existing models struggle with long-form, multi-speaker videos, especially in understanding the entire video and recognizing who says what and when. To characterize the capability limit of current omni LLMs and guide future model development, we introduce Omnilingual-MsASR, a multilingual, multimodal benchmark for long-form Multi-speaker Automatic Speech Recognition (MsASR) covering six languages, recordings up to 30 minutes, and scenarios with up to 20 speakers. Omnilingual-MsASR provides parallel audio and video inputs to evaluate models' cross-modal consistency and their ability to exploit complementary cues across modalities. Extensive evaluations of leading omni-modal LLMs reveal substantial performance bottlenecks, while their tcpWERs frequently exceed 100%. These findings highlight fine-grained temporal localization, speaker disambiguation, and cross-modal synergy as key challenges for future omni-modal foundation models. Our work is available at https://github.com/QwenLM/Omnilingua-Bench/tree/main/Omnilingua-MSpeaker.
papers.title_zh: Omnilingual-MsASR：全模态大语言模型的多模态、多语言、长时多说话人ASR基准评测
papers.abstract_zh: 全模态大语言模型（LLMs）在音频和视频理解方面已取得显著进展。然而，现有模型在处理长时、多说话人视频时仍存在困难，尤其是在理解整个视频以及识别谁在何时说了什么方面。为了刻画当前全模态LLM的能力边界并指导未来的模型发展，我们提出Omnilingual-MsASR，一个面向长时多说话人自动语音识别（MsASR）的多语言、多模态基准，涵盖六种语言、时长最长30分钟的录音以及最多包含20位说话人的场景。Omnilingual-MsASR提供并行的音频和视频输入，以评估模型的跨模态一致性及其利用跨模态互补线索的能力。对领先全模态LLM的广泛评估揭示了显著的性能瓶颈，而其tcpWER经常超过100%。这些发现凸显了细粒度时间定位、说话人消歧和跨模态协同是未来全模态基础模型的关键挑战。我们的工作可在https://github.com/QwenLM/Omnilingua-Bench/tree/main/Omnilingua-MSpeaker获取。

papers.title: OmniSimulator: Aligning Small Language Models for Authentic Heterogeneous Behavior Modeling
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential as general-purpose user simulators for interactive systems. Prior studies have demonstrated that training on high-quality data can substantially improve model reasoning and downstream task performance. However, the upper bound of user simulation is still constrained by the model's reasoning paradigm: native chain-of-thought often degenerates into shallow pattern matching and fails to adequately model the behavioral factors underlying real user decisions. In this paper, we propose OmniSimulator, a novel training framework designed to improve the predictive ability of small LLMs for realistic user simulation on short-video platform environments. Specifically, OmniSimulator organizes behavior-oriented reasoning through a structured schema with five dimensions, carefully selects data from real user-behavior scenarios, and introduces a teacher model to generate high-quality reasoning traces under the proposed schema, helping small models learn behavior-relevant reasoning patterns rather than relying on superficial behavioral correlations. Based on this process, we construct 9,881 high-quality training instances from three months of historical interaction trajectories of 200 real users, averaging about 50 distilled examples per user. Experimental results show that OmniSimulator improves the average score of Qwen3-8B by 34.33%, achieves performance competitive with Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and supports smaller-scale, self-hosted deployment. These results suggest that learning structured behavior-oriented reasoning patterns is a promising direction towards scalable and high-fidelity LLM-based user simulation.
papers.title_zh: OmniSimulator：对齐小型语言模型以实现真实的异构行为建模
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）作为交互系统的通用用户模拟器已展现出巨大潜力。先前研究表明，在高质量数据上训练可以显著提升模型推理和下游任务性能。然而，用户模拟的上限仍受模型推理范式的制约：原生思维链常常退化为浅层模式匹配，无法充分建模真实用户决策背后的行为因素。本文提出 OmniSimulator，一种新的训练框架，旨在提升小型 LLM 在短视频平台环境中进行真实用户模拟的预测能力。具体而言，OmniSimulator 通过包含五个维度的结构化模式组织面向行为的推理，从真实用户行为场景中精心选择数据，并引入教师模型在所提出的模式下生成高质量推理轨迹，帮助小模型学习与行为相关的推理模式，而不是依赖表层的行为相关性。基于这一过程，我们从 200 名真实用户三个月的历史交互轨迹中构建了 9,881 条高质量训练实例，平均每名用户约 50 个蒸馏示例。实验结果表明，OmniSimulator 将 Qwen3-8B 的平均得分提升了 34.33%，达到与 Claude-Sonnet-4.5 竞争的性能，并支持更小规模的自托管部署。这些结果表明，学习结构化的面向行为的推理模式是迈向可扩展且高保真、基于 LLM 的用户模拟的一个有前景的方向。

papers.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
papers.summary: Codes of professional ethics guide and restrict specialists, who increasingly work with assistants built on large language models. Such an assistant can breach the user's code, or help the user breach it, without the user noticing. Evaluations reporting broad categories of harm cannot show how often this happens or which provision is breached. TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests conflicting with clauses of fifteen Russian-language professional codes with benign twins that differ only in the legitimacy of what is asked. An automated pipeline generates the tasks from the text of a code, so the corpus grows with every code added and a provision yields new tasks on every run. It also produced tasks and human-validated verdicts from two English codes of other jurisdictions. In human validation of the frozen pipeline, specialists rated 0.995 of the conflicting tasks plausible, and the model judge agreed with the adjudicated label at Gwet's AC1 of at least 0.894 on 1,860 elements. We evaluated fourteen model and reasoning-mode combinations on whether they produce the conflicting text, decline or warn. Eleven of the fourteen produce conflicting content on most such requests, mostly without a warning, and nearly three warnings in four accompany conflicting content. The models that conform more do so by declining while still serving the legitimate twin, and enabling reasoning halved the refusals of two models. We hope the dataset and pipeline will help evaluate how language models observe professional norms and let diagnostic datasets be built for particular professions and organisations.
papers.title_zh: TenetBench：一个条款锚定的俄语语料库，用于依据专业伦理准则评估语言模型
papers.abstract_zh: 专业伦理准则指导和约束专业人员，而这些专业人员越来越多地使用基于大语言模型构建的助手开展工作。此类助手可能在用户未察觉的情况下违反用户所遵循的准则，或帮助用户违反该准则。报告宽泛危害类别的评估无法显示这种情况发生的频率，也无法显示哪一条款被违反。TenetBench 将 3,433 个与十五部俄语专业准则的条款相冲突的请求，与仅在被请求内容的合法性上有所不同的良性孪生请求配对。一个自动化流水线从准则文本生成任务，因此每添加一部准则，语料库就会增长，而且每运行一次，一个条款都会产生新任务。它还从其他司法管辖区的两部英语准则中生成任务和经人工验证的判定结果。在对冻结流水线进行的人工验证中，专家将冲突任务中的 0.995 评为合理，并且模型评判者在 1,860 个元素上与裁定标签的一致程度达到至少 0.894 的 Gwet's AC1。我们评估了十四种模型与推理模式组合，考察它们是生成冲突文本、拒绝还是警告。十四种组合中有十一种在大多数此类请求上生成冲突内容，且大多没有警告，并且每四个警告中近三个伴随冲突内容。更合规的模型通过拒绝来实现这一点，同时仍然服务合法的孪生请求；而启用推理使两个模型的拒绝率减半。我们希望该数据集和流水线将有助于评估语言模型如何遵守专业规范，并使能够为特定专业和组织构建诊断性数据集。

papers.title: A Strong MoE Is All You Need for Process Supervision
papers.summary: Process reward models (PRMs) provide fine-grained supervision for multi-step reasoning, yet obtaining reliable process labels remains a central bottleneck. Existing approaches typically rely on human annotation, rollout-based estimation, or auxiliary verification. In this work, we explore a different source of process supervision natively exposed by Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models: expert routing. We show that simple routing statistics provide an intrinsic process-confidence signal that is competitive with conventional output-logit confidence. Building on this observation, we construct routing confidence by combining overall routing mass, head routing mass, and within-step routing variation, and introduce RoCo-Rethink, which identifies the least confident reasoning step and selectively regenerates the subsequent trajectory. We further introduce RoCo-PRM, which uses a strong MoE to automatically annotate reasoning trajectories with routing-derived step scores and distills them into a standalone PRM. Across multiple MoE architectures and diverse reasoning tasks, both RoCo-Rethink and RoCo-PRM consistently outperform strong baselines, while RoCo-PRM transfers effectively across both model architectures and tasks. Our findings suggest that expert routing is more than a computational dispatch mechanism: it provides an architecture-native source of process supervision for reasoning.

papers.title: Keeping Time vs. Understanding Time: Neither Alone Explains Temporal Reasoning in LLMs
papers.summary: Temporal reasoning is widely assumed to decompose into two modes: temporal arithmetic (date and time calculations), and temporal semantics (understanding temporal and causal relations). This dichotomy shapes how benchmarks are designed, how models are trained, and how progress is measured, yet its empirical validity has never been directly tested. We provide two lines of evidence that challenge it. First, we test whether tasks labelled as arithmetic or semantic by the benchmarks support transferable gains within their purported mode. Finetuning on these subsets yields predominantly dataset-specific gains ($+6.8$ to $+23.1$ percentage points), while transfer to a different dataset in the same mode ranges from $-3.2$ to $+1.1$ percentage points. Across the two benchmark families used in the transfer analysis, this pattern provides little evidence of coherent, transferable temporal abilities. Second, using cognitive-demand-based model evaluation, we examine which capabilities actually drive performance on these benchmarks. We find that quantitative and logical reasoning, the assumed proxies for temporal arithmetic and temporal semantics, are not the primary drivers; knowledge is. Together, these findings show that current temporal reasoning benchmarks do not cleanly realise the arithmetic-semantics distinction and instead largely reward models for remembering how time typically works.

papers.title: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
papers.summary: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), recent studies have shown that final answers do not always depend on the generated rationales. In particular, LLMs may rely on query-specific shortcuts rather than the information provided by their reasoning steps. In this paper, we investigate whether context-aware decoding (CAD), an existing contrastive decoding method, can mitigate such shortcut behavior when applied to CoT reasoning. We study this application as Rationale Contrastive Decoding (RCD), which contrasts the next-token distributions conditioned on the query with and without its rationale, amplifying tokens whose likelihood increases due to the rationale. We provide a theoretical interpretation of this decoding rule via a KL-regularized reward-maximization objective. Experiments across five reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that RCD improves answer accuracy over standard CoT. Furthermore, intervention analyses using ground-truth and random rationales reveal that RCD increases the behavioral dependence of final answers on the rationale content. Our findings suggest that contrastive decoding offers a simple, training-free approach to mitigating query shortcuts.
papers.title_zh: 利用上下文感知解码缓解思维链中的查询捷径
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管思维链（Chain-of-Thought, CoT）提示提升了大语言模型（LLMs）的推理性能，但近期研究表明，最终答案并不总是依赖于生成的推理理由。具体而言，LLMs 可能依赖于查询特定的捷径，而不是其推理步骤所提供的信息。在本文中，我们研究上下文感知解码（CAD）——一种现有的对比解码方法——在应用于 CoT 推理时，是否能够缓解这种捷径行为。我们将这一应用作为理由对比解码（Rationale Contrastive Decoding, RCD）来研究，它对比在查询条件下、带有和不带有其理由时的下一词元分布，放大因该理由而似然增大的词元。我们通过一个 KL 正则化的奖励最大化目标，对该解码规则提供了理论解释。在五个推理基准上的实验表明，RCD 相比标准 CoT 提高了答案准确率。此外，使用真实理由和随机理由进行的干预分析表明，RCD 增强了最终答案在行为上对理由内容的依赖。我们的发现表明，对比解码为缓解查询捷径提供了一种简单、无需训练的方法。

papers.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by employing a compact draft model to propose candidate tokens that are verified in parallel by a target model. Conventional training relies on soft-label distillation, which forces the draft model to mimic the target's full output distribution, including high-entropy regions that degrade acceptance rates and increase early rejection risk. We propose RCSD (Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Speculative Decoding), a training framework that aligns draft model optimization with the system-level objective of maximizing acceptance length. RCSD leverages naturally occurring accepted and rejected sequences during speculative inference to construct implicit preference pairs, with masked loss to avoid penalizing target-aligned tokens. Evaluated across multiple benchmarks, RCSD improves average acceptance length by 35% over HASS and achieves 1.35x faster end-to-end inference than HASS on practical workloads, without compromising generation quality.
papers.title_zh: RCSD：面向领域特定投机解码的强化与持续学习
papers.abstract_zh: 投机解码通过采用一个紧凑的草稿模型来提出候选 token，并由目标模型并行验证这些候选 token，从而加速大语言模型推理。传统训练依赖软标签蒸馏，这迫使草稿模型模仿目标的完整输出分布，包括会降低接受率并增加早期拒绝风险的高熵区域。我们提出 RCSD（面向投机解码的强化与持续学习），这是一个使草稿模型优化与最大化接受长度的系统级目标相对齐的训练框架。RCSD 利用投机推理过程中自然出现的被接受和被拒绝序列来构造隐式偏好对，并采用掩码损失以避免惩罚与目标对齐的 token。在多个基准上的评估表明，RCSD 相比 HASS 将平均接受长度提升了 35%，并在实际工作负载上实现了比 HASS 快 1.35 倍的端到端推理速度，同时不损害生成质量。

papers.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
papers.summary: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time. Storing the state at lower precision therefore lets more sequences share an accelerator. Existing state quantizers round the state after every generated token and report that four bits lose accuracy unless the bit width is raised or the model is fine-tuned.\par We introduce PACE, a post-hoc four-bit state quantizer. PACE rounds the state only once every few generated tokens, as chunked kernels already do once per chunk during prefill, and keeps the tokens generated in between in a small buffer. Rounding less often reduces the error that accumulates in the state. Additionally, we find that the large entries of the gated-delta state gather in columns, because some channels of the update written at each token remain large across many tokens. PACE therefore shares each quantization scale within one column. It also keeps the heads that retain rounding error longest at eight bits. On four hybrid models from 4B to 35B parameters, PACE with mixed four- and eight-bit heads is competitive with eight-bit DAMP on the three larger models at about two thirds of its memory, PACE with four-bit heads throughout scores higher than Q-Mamba at equal memory, and rounding every few tokens preserves the decoding speedup of the buffer.

papers.title: A Diagnostic Study of Faithfulness in Diffusion Language Models for Table-to-Text Generation
papers.summary: Diffusion language models generate by iteratively denoising a masked sequence under bidirectional attention, without the strict left-to-right commitment of autoregressive decoding. Whether this difference affects how reliably they remain grounded in structured inputs is largely unexplored. We study this question in table-to-text generation using ToTTo, where highlighted source cells make factual grounding directly testable. We compare the masked diffusion models MDLM and LLaDA with GPT-2 and GPT-Neo under an identical retrieval-based few-shot protocol, together with a QLoRA-adapted LLaDA, and we score reference similarity and source grounding as separate axes. The two pull apart. Within LLaDA, additional demonstrations raise BLEU from 11.3 to 22.0 while NLI entailment against the source table falls from 0.78 to 0.52; QLoRA reaches the best BLEU of the study, 24.15, and grounds no better for it. Manual annotation shows the failure modes differ in kind: the autoregressive baselines tend to wander off the table, while LLaDA-based models more often stay on topic and swap out individual entities. Reference-based metrics alone are insufficient to assess faithfulness in table-to-text generation.
papers.title_zh: 扩散语言模型在表格到文本生成中忠实性的诊断研究
papers.abstract_zh: 扩散语言模型通过在双向注意力下对掩码序列进行迭代去噪来生成，而不具有自回归解码中严格的从左到右承诺。这一差异是否会影响它们可靠地以结构化输入为依据，在很大程度上仍未得到探索。我们使用 ToTTo 在表格到文本生成中研究这一问题，其中被高亮的源单元格使事实性依据可以直接检验。我们在相同的基于检索的少样本协议下，将掩码扩散模型 MDLM 和 LLaDA 与 GPT-2 和 GPT-Neo 进行比较，并同时比较一个经 QLoRA 适配的 LLaDA，且我们将参考相似度和源依据作为两个独立的轴进行评分。二者分离开来。在 LLaDA 内部，增加示范使 BLEU 从 11.3 提高到 22.0，而针对源表格的 NLI 蕴含度从 0.78 下降到 0.52；QLoRA 达到本研究最高的 BLEU，24.15，但其依据性并未因此更好。人工标注显示失败模式在类型上不同：自回归基线倾向于偏离表格，而基于 LLaDA 的模型更常保持主题不变并替换个别实体。仅靠基于参考的指标不足以评估表格到文本生成中的忠实性。

papers.title: Overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1: Patient-Specific Phenotype Concept Recognition in Full-Text Biomedical Literature
papers.summary: Automatic phenotype information extraction plays an important role in rare disease diagnosis, genotype-phenotype analysis, and precision medicine. However, accurately identifying phenotype concepts and determining their associations with specific patients remain challenging, particularly in full-text biomedical articles involving multiple patients and complex clinical descriptions. This paper presents an overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1, which aims to promote the development of methods for patient-specific phenotype concept recognition from full-text biomedical literature. The task consists of two subtasks: full-text phenotype concept recognition and patient-specific phenotype association. For this evaluation, we used 200 annotated full-text biomedical articles from the PatientPheX dataset, containing 506 patients, 15,193 phenotype mentions, and 5,656 patient-phenotype associations. A total of 455 teams registered for the competition, with 189 and 103 valid submissions received on the Phase A and Phase B leaderboards, respectively. The best-performing system achieved an overall score of 0.7389 on the final test set, outperforming the baseline by 8.37 percentage points. The top-performing teams explored diverse approaches combining biomedical language models, large language models (LLMs), and ensemble strategies. The evaluation results highlight both the potential of these approaches and the remaining challenges in patient attribution and phenotype normalization from full-text biomedical literature. The post-evaluation phase remains open at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/competition/entrance/532512.
papers.title_zh: CHIP 2026 共享任务 1 概述：全文生物医学文献中的患者特异性表型概念识别
papers.abstract_zh: 自动表型信息抽取在罕见病诊断、基因型-表型分析和精准医疗中发挥着重要作用。然而，准确识别表型概念并确定其与特定患者的关联仍然具有挑战性，特别是在涉及多名患者和复杂临床描述的全文生物医学文章中。本文概述了 CHIP 2026 共享任务 1，该任务旨在促进从全文生物医学文献中进行患者特异性表型概念识别的方法发展。该任务包含两个子任务：全文表型概念识别和患者特异性表型关联。在本次评估中，我们使用了来自 PatientPheX 数据集的 200 篇带标注的全文生物医学文章，其中包含 506 名患者、15,193 个表型提及和 5,656 个患者-表型关联。共有 455 支队伍注册参赛，A阶段和B阶段排行榜分别收到 189 份和 103 份有效提交。表现最佳的系统在最终测试集上取得了 0.7389 的总体得分，比基线高出 8.37 个百分点。表现最好的队伍探索了结合生物医学语言模型、大语言模型（LLMs）和集成策略的多种方法。评估结果既凸显了这些方法的潜力，也凸显了从全文生物医学文献中进行患者归因和表型规范化方面仍然存在的挑战。赛后评估阶段仍在 https://tianchi.aliyun.com/competition/entrance/532512 开放。

papers.title: LLMs as survey respondents: Comparison to simple semantic baselines
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have been explored as surrogates for human survey respondents. A more promising application is data augmentation, where LLMs predict new responses from partial human data. However, the semantic similarity between questionnaire items is a known source of correlation between answers. It is thus unclear whether LLMs actually infer meaningful relationships between question-response pairs, or use surface-level comparison between questions as a heuristic. To assess this, we evaluated how three LLMs can predict responses to held-out items in two surveys measuring attitudes toward automated or light-electric vehicles, based on varying proportions of known responses. Performance was compared to two baselines, where new responses were derived by maximizing embedding-similarity to a prior response. While LLMs mostly predicted human responses better than baselines, their performance consistently declined with a lower share of known responses, even aligning with the baseline in one survey. Our results show that LLMs' capacities for augmenting replies varied across surveys, and can revert to the same levels as simpler embedding similarity baselines when less data is available.
papers.title_zh: LLMs作为调查受访者：与简单语义基线的比较
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）已被探索作为人类调查受访者的替代者。一个更有前景的应用是数据增强，其中LLMs根据部分人类数据预测新的回答。然而，问卷条目之间的语义相似性是答案之间相关性的一个已知来源。因此，尚不清楚LLMs究竟是实际推断问题-回答对之间的有意义关系，还是将问题之间的表面层面比较作为一种启发式方法。为评估这一点，我们评估了三个LLMs在两项测量对自动化车辆或轻型电动汽车态度的调查中，基于不同比例的已知回答，如何预测对留出条目的回答。我们将性能与两个基线进行比较，其中新回答是通过最大化与先前回答的嵌入相似度得出的。尽管LLMs大多比基线更好地预测了人类回答，但随着已知回答比例的降低，它们的性能持续下降，在一项调查中甚至与基线持平。我们的结果表明，LLMs增强回答的能力在不同调查中有所不同，并且在可用数据较少时可能回落到与更简单的嵌入相似度基线相同的水平。

papers.title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
papers.summary: The deployment of small and quantized language models in resource-constrained settings raises an important fairness question: when a compressed model produces fewer biased responses, does this reflect fairer behavior or greater abstention? We study this problem in Question Answering (QA) using the BBQ benchmark across multiple model sizes and quantization settings from Qwen3, Gemma-3, and SmolLM2. We also examine whether the observed trends remain stable across alternative prompt formulations and when the ``Unknown'' option is removed in a forced-choice setting. Our results show that larger models achieved higher QA accuracy, but bias showed no simple scaling trend and quantization effects varied across configurations. Notably, 20 of the 26 configurations with fewer biased responses also show increased over-abstention, indicating that lower observed bias can partly reflect greater abstention. These findings show that lower observed bias can partly reflect greater abstention, and that fairness evaluation should consider biased responses, abstention, prompt formulation, and answer-option design jointly.

papers.title: Uni-Mem: Learning a Long-Horizon Agentic Memory Manager with Unified Online Policy Optimization
papers.summary: Long-term agent memory is shifting from predefined workflows toward learnable policies for memory construction and retrieval. Existing learning-based methods either optimize construction alone or combine retrieval-side online reinforcement learning (RL) with offline construction supervision, limiting co-adaptation between the two stages. In this paper, we explore end-to-end online RL for a unified memory manager (Uni-Mem) that learns both capabilities under a shared policy. However, joint optimization with existing RL algorithms such as GRPO faces confounded group comparisons and sparse feedback over long memory-management trajectories. To this end, we propose Stage-Decoupled GRPO, which alternates construction and retrieval optimization while controlling variation from the other stage within each rollout group, yielding stage-specific learning signals. We further introduce Event-Wise Credit Assignment (ECA), which localizes feedback to responsible events and propagates event-level advantages to their constituent operations. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval show that Uni-Mem outperforms the strongest RL-based memory, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly learning memory construction and retrieval via Stage-Decoupled GRPO and ECA.

papers.title: Scaling Multilingual Pretraining of Pixel Language Models
papers.summary: Pixel language models process text as rendered images instead of a finite vocabulary, which gives them strong cross-lingual transfer abilities. However, not much is known about how these abilities are influenced by larger-scale pretraining. In this paper, we train a family of MPIXEL models along three axes of variation: more languages, more scripts, and larger model capacity under fixed per-language compute. In evaluations on five tasks covering 83 languages, we find that scaling acts locally: each axis improves the added languages and scripts, while increased capacity mitigates the curse of multilinguality from pretraining on more languages. Transfer to unseen scripts improves with multilingual pretraining, but does not further improve with scaling. On typologically distant low-resource languages, our models outperform subword and character-level baselines across many writing systems. We also show that larger pixel models reserve more layers for visual processing, and that cross-lingual alignment weakens as more languages are added. Overall, our findings characterize how multilingual scaling improves pixel language models.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
papers.summary: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. We pre-declare three hypotheses and introduce LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG evaluation. We test 450 configurations across eight benchmarks and corpora ranging from 5K to 200K documents. Three findings emerge. First, individually strong techniques from different phases of a RAG pipeline do not necessarily compose: three retrieval techniques predict a +47% combined improvement but deliver only +17% when used together. Second, component gains stack differently for retrieval and faithfulness, and optimizing one can hurt the other. Third, the best composition changes as the corpus grows: the combination that wins on a small corpus may not remain best at large scale. These findings show that gains measured in isolation are not reliable predictors of realistic performance, and that new RAG techniques should be tested with the full surrounding stack. We call on researchers to do so and supply LASAGNA to simplify these experiments.
papers.title_zh: 检索增强生成的组合性
papers.abstract_zh: 检索增强生成（RAG）将大语言模型建立在外部知识之上。现代流水线结合了嵌入、分块、检索、重排序、查询增强、上下文压缩和智能体验证，然而这些技术通常被逐一评估。目前仍不清楚它们的孤立增益能否在组合后继续存在，检索质量和答案忠实度是否偏好相同的设计选择，以及来自小规模语料的结论能否在大规模下成立。我们预先声明了三个假设，并介绍了 LASAGNA，一个用于受控 RAG 评估的开源框架。我们在八个基准以及从 5K 到 200K 文档不等的语料上测试了 450 种配置。得出了三项发现。第一，来自 RAG 流水线不同阶段的单项强技术未必能够组合：三种检索技术预测可带来 +47% 的组合提升，但一起使用时仅带来 +17%。第二，组件增益在检索和忠实度上的叠加方式不同，优化其中一个可能会损害另一个。第三，最佳组合会随着语料规模增长而变化：在小规模语料上胜出的组合在大规模下可能不再是最佳。这些发现表明，孤立测得的增益并非现实性能的可靠预测指标，并且新的 RAG 技术应当在与完整周边技术栈一起的情况下进行测试。我们呼吁研究人员这样做，并提供 LASAGNA 来简化这些实验。

papers.title: Accept or Repair: Preserving Passage-Supported Answers in Contrastive Decoding
papers.summary: Large language models often answer from knowledge learned during training, even when a provided passage contradicts that knowledge. To address this problem, contrastive decoding contrasts the predictions under the full and a modified prompt at every token, but it also alters correct answers that the passage supports. We show that checking answers against the passage removes this trade-off. Based on this observation, we propose Accept-or-Repair (AoR), a training-free procedure. AoR keeps a sampled answer if the passage supports it. Otherwise, it tries up to two replacements with contrastive decoding, returning one as soon as it passes this check. It rejects replacements that repeat the answer generated without the passage when the passage favors another answer. Our experiments show that AoR raises the score over sampling by 12.5 points on counterfactual passages and 2.3 on ordinary ones, surpassing eight contrastive and prompting baselines on both, including when each receives the same rejection rule. Replacing only initial answers that the passage does not support improves the average score of every decoder. These results suggest that models can follow passages that contradict their knowledge while preserving accuracy on passages that agree with it. Code will be released at https://github.com/js-lee-AI/AoR.
papers.title_zh: 接受或修正：在对比解码中保留段落支持的答案
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型常常依据训练期间学到的知识作答，即使所提供的段落与该知识相矛盾。为解决这一问题，对比解码在每个token处对比完整提示与修改后提示下的预测，但它也会改变段落所支持的正确答案。我们表明，依据段落检查答案可以消除这一权衡。基于这一观察，我们提出接受或修正（Accept-or-Repair，AoR），一种无需训练的过程。如果段落支持某个采样答案，AoR就保留该答案。否则，它尝试最多两次使用对比解码进行替换，并在某个替换一旦通过该检查时立即返回该替换。当段落倾向于另一个答案时，它拒绝那些重复无段落条件下所生成答案的替换。我们的实验表明，AoR在反事实段落上将分数较采样提高12.5分，在普通段落上提高2.3分，并在两者上都超过八个对比解码与提示基线，包括当每个基线都接受相同的拒绝规则时。仅替换段落不支持的初始答案可提高每个解码器的平均分数。这些结果表明，模型能够遵循与其知识相矛盾的段落，同时保持在与知识一致的段落上的准确性。代码将发布于 https://github.com/js-lee-AI/AoR。

papers.title: Bridging Foundational and Agentic Capabilities of LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents, yet it remains unclear how their foundational capabilities translate into agentic capabilities. End-to-end scores leave unresolved whether low benchmark capability or weak deployment drives a failure, limiting actionable diagnosis. We bridge foundational and agentic capabilities through an operation-level measurement framework. We represent each model with a foundational profile derived from capability benchmarks and an operation profile derived from interaction trajectories, and define capability realization gaps as deviations of observed operation performance from predictions based on foundational capabilities. Experiments on fifteen model services in $τ^2$-Bench show that foundational profiles only partially predict agentic operations. Models with comparable profiles can differ substantially in execution, and these gaps remain consistent across task subsets. Operation profiles add information and substantially improve task-score prediction. The framework locates execution departures at the operation level to inform model development and agent evaluation. We will release our code and analysis artifacts.
papers.title_zh: 衔接大语言模型的基础能力与智能体能力
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地作为智能体被部署，但其基础能力如何转化为智能体能力仍不清楚。端到端得分无法判定失败究竟是由较低的基准能力还是由较弱的部署所驱动，这限制了可操作的诊断。我们通过一个操作级测量框架来衔接基础能力与智能体能力。我们用由能力基准推导出的基础画像和由交互轨迹推导出的操作画像来表示每个模型，并将能力实现差距定义为观测到的操作性能相对于基于基础能力所作预测的偏离。在 $τ^2$-Bench 中对十五个模型服务进行的实验表明，基础画像只能部分预测智能体操作。画像相近的模型在执行上可能差异显著，且这些差距在不同任务子集上保持一致。操作画像增加了信息，并显著提升了任务得分预测。该框架在操作层面定位执行偏离，为模型开发和智能体评估提供依据。我们将发布我们的代码和分析产物。

papers.title: ALIAS: Evaluating Performance and Memorization in LLM-Written TLA+ Specifications
papers.summary: Memorization inflates the benchmark scores of large language models (LLMs), since a model can reproduce answers it saw in training. Researchers test for it with consistent identifier renaming (CIR), which gives every identifier in a task a new name, and treat a lower score on the renamed task as evidence of recall. We test this method on the Temporal Logic of Actions Plus (TLA+) language, whose model checker acts as an oracle by confirming whether a renamed task preserves the exact behaviors of the original. Across 111 TLA+-Bench tasks, renaming lowers the correctness of Claude Opus 4.8 from 28% to 18% and of GPT-5 from 9% to 7%. Most of this decrease comes from how the test grades, which requires exact names that most descriptions never state. Grading by behavior shrinks the decrease to about 3 percentage points for Opus 4.8 and to 0 for GPT-5. In two model families fine-tuned on disjoint halves of the tasks, renaming removes about half of the training gain in likelihood and costs 4.9 percentage points (Qwen) and 1.3 percentage points (Gemma) on unseen tasks. A lower score after renaming therefore mixes memorization, name-based grading, and the cost of new names.
papers.title_zh: ALIAS：评估 LLM 编写的 TLA+ 规范中的性能与记忆
papers.abstract_zh: 记忆会抬高大型语言模型（LLM）的基准分数，因为模型能够复现其在训练中见过的答案。研究人员通过一致性标识符重命名（consistent identifier renaming，CIR）来检验这一点：该方法为任务中的每个标识符赋予新名称，并将重命名任务上更低的分数视为存在回忆的证据。我们在动作时序逻辑增强版（Temporal Logic of Actions Plus，TLA+）语言上测试了该方法；TLA+ 的模型检查器充当预言机（oracle），确认重命名后的任务是否保留了原任务的确切行为。在 111 个 TLA+-Bench 任务上，重命名将 Claude Opus 4.8 的正确率从 28% 降至 18%，并将 GPT-5 的正确率从 9% 降至 7%。这一下降的大部分来自测试的评分方式，该方式要求使用大多数描述从未给出的确切名称。按行为评分将 Opus 4.8 的下降幅度缩小到约 3 个百分点，并将 GPT-5 的下降幅度缩小到 0。在两个分别在不重叠的任务半集上微调的模型系列中，重命名消除了约一半的似然训练增益，并在未见任务上造成 4.9 个百分点（Qwen）和 1.3 个百分点（Gemma）的损失。因此，重命名后更低的分数混合了记忆、基于名称的评分以及新名称带来的代价。

papers.title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
papers.summary: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. Here we introduce DeepEvolve, a sustainable evolution agent system grounded in future event prediction, in which agents continuously interact with a dynamically evolving environment and improve by internalizing and externalizing the experience gained through these interactions. A living environment synthesizes verifiable tasks, and a recursive-evolution engine turns the reasoning trajectory behind each prediction back into capability: decoupling search from prediction adapts parameter-level evolution to the contamination-prone live environment, while distilling reusable skills lets the agent evolve from the limited live trajectories such an environment affords. On the external FutureX leaderboard, which evaluates predictions against real-world outcomes and is updated weekly, our self-improved forecaster ranked first across all systems over three consecutive weeks, achieving up to a 195% improvement in rating. On our synthesized evaluation, it ranked among the top three across four base LLMs, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 10.7 Bradley--Terry points. More broadly, these results suggest that a system built for self-improvement is best understood as an agent that co-evolves with a genuinely living, open-ended environment, pointing to a shift in AI from training static models on fixed data toward cultivating agents that grow stronger from their own experience, with such an open world as the indispensable basis of that growth.

papers.title: Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI?
papers.summary: Asked what to study, which career to pursue, or what product to build, large language models (LLMs) often recommend AI-related options. We ask where this tendency comes from by comparing models before and after fine-tuning and by varying how questions are asked. First, pretrained models already include explicit AI/ML terms in the recommendations of 27% of their responses, and their released instruction-tuned versions do so in 59%. Second, fine-tuning models ourselves shows that this rise is not inevitable: general instruction tuning leaves the rate unchanged, but removing the 7% of instruction examples that concern AI cuts it by 14 percentage points, below the level of the pretrained models it starts from. Data rewarding helpfulness raise it by 9 points, while data ranked by the preferences of diverse simulated users lower it by 9. Finally, with models held fixed, asking for the "best" option or for what to do "right now" raises the rate by 8 and 18 points, whereas telling the model it is an AI advisor adds 4. Overall, the tendency starts in pretraining, and what models learn afterward, together with how a question is phrased, decides how strongly it appears.
papers.title_zh: 大语言模型在哪里学会推荐 AI？
papers.abstract_zh: 当被问及该学什么、该从事什么职业或该构建什么产品时，大语言模型（LLMs）常常推荐与 AI 相关的选项。我们通过比较微调前后的模型以及改变提问方式，来探究这种倾向来自何处。首先，预训练模型在其 27% 的回复的推荐中已经包含明确的 AI/ML 术语，而其发布的指令微调版本这一比例为 59%。其次，我们自己对模型进行微调表明，这种上升并非不可避免：通用指令微调使该比率保持不变，但移除涉及 AI 的那 7% 指令示例会使其降低 14 个百分点，低于其起始预训练模型的水平。奖励有用性的数据使其提高 9 个百分点，而按多样化模拟用户偏好排序的数据使其降低 9 个百分点。最后，在模型固定的情况下，询问“最佳”选项或“现在”该做什么会使该比率分别提高 8 和 18 个百分点，而告诉模型它是一名 AI 顾问则增加 4 个百分点。总体而言，这种倾向始于预训练，而模型此后学到的东西，连同问题的措辞方式，决定了它显现的强度。

papers.title: MAPS: Macro-Adaptive Parallel Reasoning for Regulating Search Momentum in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) by retrieving external knowledge. Recently, some RAG methods interleave reasoning and retrieval, enabling LLMs to progressively generate sub-queries and retrieve external knowledge. However, these methods may suffer from redundant or ineffective sub-queries and insufficiently diverse query exploration. Moreover, due to the tightly interleaved nature of reasoning and retrieval, it remains unclear how the evolving reasoning process influences query intent. To characterize the evolution of query intent during reasoning, we introduce search momentum, which captures the accumulated retrieval tendency induced by historical changes in generated sub-queries along the reasoning trajectory. Through momentum-based analysis, we find that the query generation process tends to continuously evolve along existing retrieval trajectories. Based on this observation, we propose MAPS, a Macro-Adaptive Parallel Reasoning framework for regulating search momentum and mitigating query-intent drift. MAPS first retains the retrieved knowledge and a refined reasoning state, thereby reducing the influence of historical reasoning trajectories on subsequent sub-query generation. Subsequently, MAPS extends the conventional sequential reasoning process into a parallel reasoning paradigm. At each iteration, MAPS identifies complementary retrieval directions, generates corresponding sub-queries for parallel retrieval, and consolidates the retrieved evidence to update the knowledge and reasoning states. Experiments on six question-answering benchmarks demonstrate that MAPS consistently outperforms representative RAG methods across different backbone models. All code and resources are available at https://github.com/NEUIR/MAPS.
papers.title_zh: MAPS：用于调控检索增强生成中搜索动量的宏观自适应并行推理
papers.abstract_zh: 检索增强生成（RAG）通过检索外部知识来提升大语言模型（LLMs）的性能。最近，一些RAG方法将推理与检索交织进行，使LLMs能够逐步生成子查询并检索外部知识。然而，这些方法可能面临子查询冗余或无效以及查询探索多样性不足的问题。此外，由于推理与检索紧密交织的本质，不断演化的推理过程如何影响查询意图仍不清楚。为了刻画推理过程中查询意图的演化，我们引入了搜索动量，它刻画了沿推理轨迹生成的子查询的历史变化所诱发的累积检索趋势。通过基于动量的分析，我们发现查询生成过程倾向于沿现有检索轨迹持续演化。基于这一观察，我们提出了MAPS，一个用于调控搜索动量并缓解查询意图漂移的宏观自适应并行推理框架。MAPS首先保留已检索知识和精炼后的推理状态，从而降低历史推理轨迹对后续子查询生成的影响。随后，MAPS将传统的顺序推理过程扩展为并行推理范式。在每次迭代中，MAPS识别互补的检索方向，生成相应的子查询以进行并行检索，并整合检索到的证据以更新知识和推理状态。在六个问答基准上的实验表明，MAPS在不同骨干模型上始终优于具有代表性的RAG方法。所有代码和资源均可在 https://github.com/NEUIR/MAPS 获取。

papers.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
papers.summary: Agent memory systems such as Mem0 and Zep decide what to keep before any question arrives; coding agents keep the raw history and let the model search it with its own tools. We ask whether designed memory still helps once the model is strong enough to search for itself. On one LoCoMo conversation (419 turns, 152 questions), we run four memory methods (full context, BM25, Mem0, Zep) and three coding agents (Pi, Codex, Claude Code), each with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5, and record what every rollout costs. This is a short empirical study, with one conversation and one run per cell. Agent memory is a costly patch for a weak model: Mem0 beats full context only with GPT-4o-mini, and its build alone costs more than a whole full-context rollout. Agent memory also has a ceiling, set by the model that writes it: a stronger reader does not recover what a weaker writer left out. With Claude Opus 5.5, Pi tops the cost-accuracy frontier, scoring 99% for less than half the cost of full context; its one miss is a wrong answer key. Part of that lead comes from photo captions that only the agents could read: on the 88 questions whose evidence has no photo, Pi and full context differ by one answer.

papers.title: S-EDL: Eliciting Self-Evidence from Sequence Likelihoods for Semantic Calibration of LLMs
papers.summary: Calibrating large language models (LLMs) in open-ended generation is uniquely challenging because many distinct token sequences can express the same underlying meaning. Prior calibration techniques target either fixed-set classification confidence or the binary correctness of individual strings, making them inherently ill-suited for the dynamic, multi-string nature of open-ended semantic outcomes. To bridge this gap, we introduce S-EDL, a novel evidential method that natively optimizes LLMs for semantic calibration. By eliciting evidence from the sequence likelihoods of the model itself, S-EDL constructs a differentiable Dirichlet prior over prompt-specific semantic classes. Optimizing the evidential loss under this prior yields a calibration-aware training signal over variable semantic classes, completely bypassing the need for fixed multiple-choice options. Evaluations across four open-ended benchmarks and three models demonstrate that S-EDL substantially reduces semantic calibration error while improving accuracy. By aligning generative likelihoods with semantic correctness, this work establishes a framework for deploying trustworthy LLMs in complex, open-ended applications. Code is available at: https://github.com/sandylaker/s-edl.
papers.title_zh: S-EDL：从序列似然中引出自我证据以实现大语言模型的语义校准
papers.abstract_zh: 在开放式生成中校准大语言模型（LLMs）具有独特挑战性，因为许多不同的词元序列可以表达相同的潜在含义。先前的校准技术要么针对固定集合分类置信度，要么针对单个字符串的二元正确性，这使它们本质上不适合开放式语义结果所具有的动态、多字符串特性。为弥合这一差距，我们提出 S-EDL，一种新颖的证据式方法，它原生地优化 LLMs 以实现语义校准。通过从模型自身的序列似然中引出证据，S-EDL 在提示特定的语义类别上构建可微的狄利克雷先验。在该先验下优化证据损失，可在可变的语义类别上产生校准感知的训练信号，从而完全绕过对固定多项选择选项的需求。在四个开放式基准和三个模型上的评估表明，S-EDL 在提高准确率的同时大幅降低了语义校准误差。通过将生成似然与语义正确性对齐，这项工作建立了一个在复杂开放式应用中部署可信 LLMs 的框架。代码可在以下地址获取：https://github.com/sandylaker/s-edl。

papers.title: Every Part Has Its Role: Part-of-Speech Effects in LLM Post-Training
papers.summary: Large language models are typically trained with next-token prediction (NTP), which rewards predicting specific tokens rather than explicitly accounting for the semantic similarities between different words or expressions. Prior work has addressed this limitation by augmenting training data with minimally varying sentences that replace a target word with conceptually related alternatives, e.g., "The tired coach ran home" $\rightarrow$ {"The tired trainer ran home", "The tired instructor ran home", ...}. Such concept augmentation improves performance, but it remains unclear whether its effectiveness depends on where in the sentence the concept is expressed. We reproduce and extend prior work $\textit{beyond nouns}$ to verbs and adjectives, asking whether the part of speech (POS) carrying the concept signal affects perplexity and downstream performance. We find different patterns across evaluation settings: concept augmentation improves perplexity most consistently on news, independent of the POS used, whereas verbs provide the most reliable downstream gains. Despite these behavioral differences, representational analyses using CKA and linear probing show that the conditions yielding the largest downstream gains are not necessarily those that most alter the model's internal representations. Together, these results suggest that the effectiveness of concept augmentation depends on where and how conceptual information is introduced during training.
papers.title_zh: 每一部分都有其作用：LLM 后训练中的词性效应
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型通常使用下一词元预测（NTP）进行训练，这种训练奖励的是预测特定词元，而不是显式考虑不同词语或表达之间的语义相似性。已有工作通过用仅有最小变化的句子增强训练数据来应对这一局限，这些句子将一个目标词替换为概念上相关的替代词，例如，“疲惫的教练跑回了家” $\rightarrow$ {“疲惫的训练员跑回了家”，“疲惫的指导者跑回了家”，...}。这种概念增强提升了性能，但其有效性是否取决于概念在句子中被表达的位置，仍不清楚。我们复现并扩展了先前的工作 $\textit{beyond nouns}$，将其扩展到动词和形容词，考察承载概念信号的词性（POS）是否影响困惑度和下游性能。我们在不同评估设置中发现了不同的模式：概念增强在新闻文本上最稳定地改善困惑度，且与所使用的词性无关，而动词则提供最可靠的下游性能提升。尽管存在这些行为差异，使用 CKA 和线性探测进行的表征分析表明，产生最大下游性能提升的条件未必是那些最改变模型内部表征的条件。总之，这些结果表明，概念增强的有效性取决于概念信息在训练期间被引入的位置和方式。

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of Learner Errors on Social Bias in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Existing social bias benchmarks evaluate large language models mostly on fluent, well-formed English, reflecting native speaker usage and leaving non-native writers unrepresented. To address this gap, we investigate how grammatical errors by non-native writers affect social bias. We develop a controlled framework that injects common learner errors into prompts and apply it to three bias benchmarks covering stereotype alignment and demographic preference across gender, race, and religion. We find that grammatical errors increase bias, and the effect grows with the error rate. Among the four common error types we consider, preposition errors produce the largest and most consistent increase in stereotype alignment. Our analysis suggests that errors increase bias when they are more likely to interfere with comprehension. Finally, fine-tuning on erroneous texts reduces the bias increase caused by grammatical errors. Our findings show that bias evaluations based exclusively on well-formed prompts may underestimate the bias experienced by users whose English contains grammatical errors.
papers.title_zh: 探究学习者错误对大语言模型中社会偏见的影响
papers.abstract_zh: 现有的社会偏见基准主要在流利、格式良好的英语上评估大语言模型，这反映了母语者的用法，并使非母语写作者未被代表。为弥补这一空白，我们研究非母语写作者的语法错误如何影响社会偏见。我们开发了一个受控框架，将常见的学习者错误注入提示中，并将其应用于三个偏见基准，这些基准涵盖性别、种族和宗教方面的刻板印象对齐和人口统计学偏好。我们发现语法错误会增加偏见，而且这种效应随错误率上升而增强。在我们考虑的四种常见错误类型中，介词错误在刻板印象对齐方面产生最大且最一致的增加。我们的分析表明，当错误更可能干扰理解时，它们会增加偏见。最后，在含有错误的文本上进行微调可减少由语法错误引起的偏见增加。我们的发现表明，仅基于格式良好提示的偏见评估可能低估英语包含语法错误的用户所经历的偏见。

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Detecting Satirical Code-Mixed Sentences
papers.summary: Code-switching is a natural linguistic phenomenon, yet its impact on high-level reasoning tasks remains largely unexplored in under-resourced languages like Romanian. Natural language processing tasks, such as satire detection, rely heavily on nuanced cultural and syntactic cues that large language models struggle to capture. In this paper, we investigate four methods (i.e., random replacement, phrase translation, dependency parsing, and large language models) for generating synthetic code-mixed Romanian sentences with English, German, French, and Italian. We start with an existing dataset for satire detection, compiled from Romanian news articles and annotated at the sentence level by humans, and augment it with over 600k samples, namely CS-SeLeRoSa. We provide an in-depth analysis of the dataset generation process. Then, we evaluate several multilingual large language models across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and fine-tuning regimes on both the synthetic corpus and a human-adjudicated gold benchmark, namely CS-SeLeRoSa-Gold. While older open models suffer substantial degradation (dropping to 37%-55% macro-F1), newer models like Gemma 4 31B achieve 68.1% zero-shot, rivaling frontier models like GPT-5 mini (69.5%).
